 海棠PT是一个什么样的站？ 
我们是一个主打国粹曲艺的私人分享PT站点.
 我从哪里可以联系到海棠PT的管理组？ 
QQ群：594387685 Email:ssr64953@qq.com 网站导航栏点击 -[私信管理]
 用户信息 - 
 我注册了一个账号但是却没有收到验证邮件！ 
这很有可能是Tracker所在的服务器网络出现了问题。你可以填写 这个表格 让服务器重发验证邮件。
通常没有得到确认的注册帐户会在24小时后被删除，所以你可以在第二天重试。需要注意的是，如果你第一次没有收到确认信，第二次有很大的可能仍然无法收到确认信，所以换一个E-mail地址是一个不错的主意。
 我忘记了我的用户名/密码了，能帮我找回来么？ 
请使用注册邮箱发送找回密码请求到Email：ssr64953@qq.com
 我可以给我的账号改个名字么？ 
我们并不支持给账号改名。
 你可以删除一个（已确认的）账号么？ 
我们一般不提供该类服务，所以不要请求删除任何一个被你邀请的帐号。
 那么，什么是我的分享率（Ratio）？ 
就在页面功能分区的下面。
区分你的整体分享率和独立分享率是很重要的。整体分享率关注的是自从你加入站点以来，账号的整体上传与下载量。而独立分享率则针对每一个你正在下载或做种的文件。
你可能看到两种符号来代替数字："Inf."，这个是无限（Infinity）的缩写，意思是你的下载量为0字节，而上传量则是任意一个非零的值(上传量/下载量=无穷大)；"---"，应该被视为“不可用”，这说明了你的下载量和上传量都是0字节。(上传量/下载量=0/0 这是一个不确定的量)。

 为什么我的“可连接”是“否”？（以及为什么我需要关注这个问题？） 
Tracker服务器认为你在防火墙后，或者在NAT桥接后，并且无法接收其他Peer的连接请求。
这意味着其它的大批Peer无法连接到你，只能由你连接到他们。更糟糕的情况是，如果两个Peer都处于这样的状态，他们将完全无法连接到对方。这对于整体速度有着非常不利的影响。
对于这个问题，有以下解决方式：对于防火墙，打开用于接收连接的端口（即你在BT客户端中定义的端口）；对于NAT，你需要配置NAT服务器使用Basic NAT方式而不是NAPT（不同的路由有着不同的运行方式。翻阅你的路由文档或客服论坛。你也可以在 PortForward 找到关于此问题的大量信息）。

 最佳的尝试 
 如果你当前正下载/上传的种子并不在你的用户详情页面中，你可以等一会或者强制进行手动更新。
 确保你正确地关闭了客户端软件，否则Tracker服务器无法收到"event=completed"的信号。

 为什么我正在下载/做种的一个种子会在我的详情页面中被列出多次？ 
如果因为某些原因(比方说死机，客户端失去响应)你的客户端非正常退出并且你又重新打开它，它会被分配到一个全新的Peer ID, 这样它显示为一个全新的种子。而旧的种子将永远不会收到“event=completed”或“event=stopped”的信号，因此将一直被列出直到Tracker清理超时的Peer。 无视了它就可以了，它最后会消失的。
 为什么我已经完成/取消的种子仍然在我的详情页面里？ 
有一些客户端，比如说TorrentStorm和Nova Torrent，在取消或者完成一个任务的时候不能向Tracker服务器正确发送信号。在那样的情况下，Tracker服务器将一直保持等待信号的状态（因此会一直列出种子的状态为做种/下载的状态）直到Tracker清理超时的Peer。无视了它就可以了，它最后会消失的。
 多IP（我可以从不同的电脑登录/下载吗？） 
是的，目前Tracker服务器支持单个用户从任意个数的IP地址同时访问/下载。
然而，对于单种是有限制的。对于每个种子，最多允许3个做种的连接，最多只允许1个下载的连接（这意味着，对于某个种子你一次只能在一个地方下载）。

 "部分哈希验证出错"这条信息是什么意思？ 
BT的客户端会检查它所收到的数据的完整性。如果某一个片段在验证中出错，那么这个片段将被重新下载。偶尔的哈希验证错误是非常常见的现象，不用担心。
有些客户端有屏蔽向你发送错误数据的其他客户端的功能。如果有这个选项，最好打开它。因为这样可以保证如果某个同伴经常向你发送错误的数据时，它将会被屏蔽。
 100MB大小的种子，我怎么下了120MB的东西回来? 
参见哈希验证失败的那个问题。如果你的客户端收到了错误的数据，那么它将会重新下载这一部分，因此总下载量有可能比种子大小略微大一些。确保“屏蔽发送错误数据的客户端”的那个选项被打开了，这样可以减少额外的下载。

你的客户端向Tracker服务器报告它正在使用某个默认的BT协议端口(6881-6889)或是任何其他常见P2P端口来作为连接端口。
本站不允许这些通常被P2P协议默认使用的端口。原因是目前ISP常常对这些端口进行限速。
被屏蔽的端口如下：

 6346 - 6347

要使用我们的Tracker服务器，你必须配置你的客户端使用未在上面列出的端口范围(从49152到65535都是不错的选择，参看 IANA )。注意某些客户端，如Azureus 2.0.7.0或更高版本，对所有的种子都使用同一端口。而其他大多数客户端为每一个种子开放一个端口，你在选择端口范围应考虑到这个问题（一般来说端口范围小于10。设置一个过大的范围并不一定有好处，而且可能有安全隐患)。 
这些端口是用于同伴间通信的，而非用于客户端连接到Tracker服务器。因此这个改动并不会影响你使用其他Tracker服务器（事实上，它甚至可能 加快 所有Tracker服务器上种子的速度）。你的客户端也仍然能够连接到那些使用默认端口的同伴。如果你的客户端不支持自己自定义端口，那么换一个吧。
不要向我们询问，或者在论坛里面提问究竟应该选择什么端口。我们的用户选择的端口越随机，ISP就越难以捉摸清楚我们使用的端口，从而无法对我们的端口进行限速。如果我们只是简单地规定一个范围，那么ISP又会很快对那个范围内的端口进行限速的。
最后还要说的是，记得在你的路由和/或防火墙上打开你选择的端口，如果你有这些东西的话。
 那么这个呢？ “IO错误 - [错误号13] 许可被拒绝”？ 
如果你只是想要解决这个问题的话，重新启动你的电脑应该就可以了。否则的话，继续读下去。
IO错误指的是输入-输出错误，这是一个文件系统错误，而非来自我们的Tracker服务器。当你的客户端由于某些原因不能打开种子中未下载完成的文件时，这个错误就会发生。 通常原因是客户端的两个实例同时在运行：当上一次关闭客户端时因为某种原因它没有被真正关闭，从而始终在后台运行。因此文件被锁定，使得新的实例不能打开这个文件。
另外一个不常出现的原因是因为老旧的FAT文件系统。某些系统崩溃可能导致未下载完成的文件损坏，接着就出现了这个错误。运行一次scandisk应该可以解决这个问题。注意，只有当你使用Windows 9X操作系统（只支持FAT文件系统）或者在Windows NT/2000/XP中使用FAT文件系统的时候才比较可能出现这个问题。NTFS文件系统要健壮许多，不太可能出现这样的问题。
 什么是密钥系统？它是怎么工作的？ 
密钥系统在BT客户端连接Tracker服务器时起到验证身份的作用。每一个用户都有一个系统随机生成的密钥。当用户下载某个种子文件时，他的私人密钥被添加到种子文件的Tracker服务器URL中。通过这种方式，你可以在家中或者办公室使用不同的IP来做种某个文件。
 “Unknown passkey”这错误是咋回事？ 
首先，如果你不是我们的注册用户，将会发生这个错误。其次，有可能你没有在登录状态下从我们的网页里下载种子文件。如果是这两种情况，只要注册一个帐号或者登录后下载种子文件就可以了。
另外，当你注册了一个新用户并且开始第一次下载的时候，或者你刚刚重置了你的密钥时，也可能出现这个错误。原因是系统并非实时检查密钥的改变。如果是因为这个原因，那么就让种子任务等一会儿，最后一定能收到Tracker服务器发回的成功信息。
 什么时候我需要重置我的密钥? 
 如果你的密钥被泄漏，且别的用户正在使用这个密钥（即使用你的帐户）下载文件。在这种情况下，你能在你的详情页面看到你并未下载或上传的种子。
 当你的客户端崩溃，或者你的连接并没有正常被终止。在这样的情况下，就算你已经关闭了你的客户端，你仍然在你的详情页面看到正在上传/下载的记录。通常情况下这些“冗余种子”将在30分钟之内被自动清除，但是如果你马上继续你的下载而服务器又提示“You already are downloading the same torrent”的错误，那么你需要重置你的密钥，然后重新下载种子文件，之后继续下载过程。 
 DHT是什么？为什么一定要关闭这个功能？ 
DHT必须从你的客户端被禁止。DHT可能导致你的数据被错误地记录，可以视为一种作弊行为。任何使用DHT的用户将因作弊而被系统禁止。
幸运的是，目前Tracker服务器会自动分析用户上传的种子文件，强制去除DHT的支持。这也是为什么种子发布者必须重新下载种子才能正常做种的原因之一。
 为什么我的磁盘还有充足的空间，客户端却提示磁盘剩余空间不足？ 
很可能是因为你的磁盘分区的文件系统为FAT32，该文件系统不支持大于4GB的单个文件。如果你使用的是Windows系统，你可以在磁盘的属性中查看其文件系统信息。你可以将磁盘文件系统转换成更高级的NTFS来解决该问题。
你可以在命令行窗口使用convert命令将FAT32无损转成NTFS文件系统格式。
 命令说明 
CONVERT volume /FS:NTFS [/V] [/CvtArea:filename] [/NoSecurity] [/X]
volume 指定驱动器号(后面跟一个冒号)、装载点或卷名。
/FS:NTFS 指定要被转换成 NTFS 的卷。
/V 指定 Convert 应该用详述模式运行。
/CvtArea:filename 将根目录中的一个接续文件指定为NTFS 系统文件的占位符。
/NoSecurity 指定每个人都可以访问转换的文件和目录的安全设置。
/X 如果必要，先强行卸载卷。该卷的所有打开的句柄则无效。 
 简单说 
：
打开 命令提示符窗口。
在命令提示符窗口，请键入：
convert drive_letter:/fs:ntfs
例如：转换D盘为NTFS，可输入convert D:/fs:ntfs
 我该怎样提升下载速度？ - 
 不要马上下载新发布的种子 
下载速度主要取决于上传者/下载者比(SLR)。如果是种子是新发布的且非常受欢迎而SLR又很低的种子，下载速度低是常见的问题。
请牢记你不喜欢低速下载。所以多 上传 让别人不用忍耐同样的困扰。
由其是当你的带宽较窄时，不要马上下载新发布的种子。最好的下载速度通常在一个种子生命周期的一半时出现，此时SLR达到最大值（不过，这时下载的缺点是你的上传量不会很多。究竟如何平衡优点与缺点，取决于你自己)。
 限制上传速度 
上传速度将从以下两种方式显著影响下载速度：
 Bittorrent的同伴倾向于回馈那些给它们提上传的同伴。这就意味着如果A和B正在同时下载一个文件，而A又在高速向B传送数据，那么B将会尝试着回报A。因此高速上传将导致高速下载。
 由于TCP协议的工作方式，当A正从B下载某些东西的时候，A必须不停地向B发送成功收到B所发送来的数据的信号（被称为确认──ACK ── 某种“已收到”的信息)。如果A没有发送ACK信号，那么B将暂停向A发送数据并且进入等候状态。如果A正在全速上传，很有可能没有用来发送ACK信号的带宽，因此ACK信号被耽搁。在这种情况下，过高速度的上传导致了低速的下载。
实际的效果是以上两个原因的结合。上传速度应该在保证ACK能正常传输的前提下被设得尽量高。 一个很好的实践理论是保持上传速度在理论上限的80%。 你也可以细细研究什么是最适合你的速度（同时也请记住高速上传对于你的分享率很有帮助）。
如果你正在运行一个以上的种子任务，你应该考虑的是全局上传速度。某些客户端能限制了全局上传速度，其他的则能对每一个种子分别进行设置。了解你的客户端。如果你正在使用你的电脑做别的某些应用（比方说上网或者从FTP拖东西），也需考虑一下它们对于全局上传的影响。
 限制同时连接数 
某些操作系统（例如Windows 9X）对于大量连接数支持不完善，甚至有可能因此而崩溃。也有一些家用路由（尤其当运行着NAT以及/或者打开防火墙状态检查服务时）会因大量连接数而变得很慢或者崩溃。对于连接数没有固定的最佳值，你可以试试看60或者100。记住这些连接数是累加的，所以如果你的客户端运行了两个会话，这两个数字要加在一起。
 限制同时上传数 
上传数难道和连接数有什么不一样吗？是的，两者是不同的。连接数限制了你的客户端所能对话以及/或者下载的同伴数。上传数则限制了你的客户端实际能上传的同伴数。理想的数值一般要比连接数低许多，并且与你的物理带宽高度相关。
 那怎么办？等待一会吧 
如我们在上面所解释的，在BT下载过程中一个同伴更加倾向于回报那些上传给它的同伴。当你开始一个新的下载任务时，你没有文件片断提高给其他同伴，因此他们通常会无视你。这使得开始阶段的下载非常缓慢，由其是当你所连接到的同伴只有很少是（或者没有）做种者。一旦你获得了一些能用于共享的文件片断，下载速度会有所改观。
 为什么在我下载的时候浏览网页速度如此之慢？ 
你的下载带宽是有限的。如果你正在下载一个速度很快的种子，它几乎肯定将占满你的下载带宽。这是浏览网页显然就会变慢。很多BT客户端允许你限制下载速度，你可以试试。
浏览网页只是作为举例之一，同样的问题也会出现在游戏，即时通信软件上......
 我的网络提供商（ISP）使用了透明代理。我应该怎么做？ - 
 什么是代理？ 
基本上说，代理就是中间人。当你通过代理访问某个站点的时候，你的请求将首先被发送到代理处，然后由代理转发到你所请求的站点，而不是你直接连通到网站。下面是几种典型的代理分类（术语不是那么的规范）：
 透明代理 
 透明代理在客户端无需配置。他将自动把80端口的信息重定向到代理(有时候也作为非匿名代理的同义词)； 
 显式代理 
 浏览器必须经过配置才能使用代理； 
 匿名代理 
 代理将不会把客户标记发送至服务器端 (HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR头标志将不被发送。服务器也因此看不到你的IP)； 
 高度匿名代理 
 代理将不会把客户标记或代理标记发送至服务器端 (HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR和HTTP_VIA and HTTP_PROXY_CONNECTION头标志将不被发送。服务器看不到你的IP，甚至不知道你正在使用代理)； 
 公用 
 (不言自明了)。 
透明代理可能是匿名的，也可能是非匿名的，且匿名也有相应的等级。
 我该怎样发现自己正处于一个（透明的/匿名的）代理后面？ 
试试看 ProxyJudge 。它列出了服务器端从你这里所收到的HTTP的头标志。相关的几个标志是HTTP_CLIENT_IP，HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR和REMOTE_ADDR。
 我的“可连接”是“否”尽管我并没有NAT或者防火墙？ 
Tracker服务器在寻找你的真实IP方面非常有天赋。但是这需要代理发送HTTP头标志HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR。如果你的ISP的代理没有这么做的话，Tracker服务器将把代理的IP当作你的客户端的IP。所以当你登录之后，Tracker服务器尝试连接你的客户端来确信你没有使用NAT/防火墙，服务器实际上将试图连接代理的IP（使用你的BT客户端报告的接收连接端口）。很自然地，代理服务器并没有监听那个端口。如此连接会失败，而Tracker服务器也因此认为你使用了NAT/防火墙。
 为什么我连不上？难道我被网站屏蔽了？ - 
 也许是因为我的IP地址被列入黑名单了？ 
这个网站有屏蔽被禁用户或攻击者的IP地址的功能。该功能在Apache/PHP层面上起作用，且只能屏蔽从这些地址 登录 网站。这不会阻止你 连接 到网站，更无法从底层的协议层面进行屏蔽。即便你的地址已经被列入了黑名单，你应该仍能够通过ping/traceroute命令连同服务器。如果你不能连通服务器，那么问题的原因在别处。
如果你的IP地址因某种原因错误地被我们屏蔽了，请联系我们。
 你的ISP屏蔽了本站的地址 
首先，这一般不像你的ISP的所作所为。DNS域名解析以及/或者网络问题是常见的真凶。
对此我们无能为力。你应该联系你的ISP（或者换一个）。记住你仍然可以通过代理访问本站，参看此常见问题关于代理的部分。在这种情况下，代理是否匿名或者使用哪个监听端口都不重要了。
注意，你的“可连接状态”将因此一直被列为“否”，因为此时Tracker服务器无法检查你的BT客户端接收连接的状态。
 如果从这里找不到我的问题的解答，我该怎么办？ - 
 不妨试试这个 
用任何手段在 论坛 发帖。通常情况下你能得到友善而有用的帮助。这里给你一些基本的指导： 
 确保你的问题的确不在这篇FAQ中。这样的发帖导致的结果就是返回这篇FAQ。
 在发帖之前，看看置顶。很多时候，还没有被我们的FAQ所收录的最新的信息都可以在那里被找到。
 帮助我们也就是帮助你自己。不要仅仅说“嘿我这里出问题了！！”提供一些详情，这样我们就不用猜测或者浪费时间来询问了。你使用的是什么客户端？什么操作系统？怎样的网络设置？如果发生了错误，是什么样的具体错误信息？有问题的种子文件是哪个？你所提供的信息越多，对你的帮助也就越容易，你的帖子也就更加容易得到回复。
 不需要说的是：保持礼貌。趾高气扬得命令别人帮助你很少会有用。

 我注册了一个账号但是却没有收到验证邮件！ 
这很有可能是Tracker所在的服务器网络出现了问题。你可以填写 这个表格 让服务器重发验证邮件。
通常没有得到确认的注册帐户会在24小时后被删除，所以你可以在第二天重试。需要注意的是，如果你第一次没有收到确认信，第二次有很大的可能仍然无法收到确认信，所以换一个E-mail地址是一个不错的主意。

 那么，什么是我的分享率（Ratio）？ 
就在页面功能分区的下面。
区分你的整体分享率和独立分享率是很重要的。整体分享率关注的是自从你加入站点以来，账号的整体上传与下载量。而独立分享率则针对每一个你正在下载或做种的文件。
你可能看到两种符号来代替数字："Inf."，这个是无限（Infinity）的缩写，意思是你的下载量为0字节，而上传量则是任意一个非零的值(上传量/下载量=无穷大)；"---"，应该被视为“不可用”，这说明了你的下载量和上传量都是0字节。(上传量/下载量=0/0 这是一个不确定的量)。
 为什么我的IP地址显示在我的个人信息页面上？

 为什么我的“可连接”是“否”？（以及为什么我需要关注这个问题？） 
Tracker服务器认为你在防火墙后，或者在NAT桥接后，并且无法接收其他Peer的连接请求。
这意味着其它的大批Peer无法连接到你，只能由你连接到他们。更糟糕的情况是，如果两个Peer都处于这样的状态，他们将完全无法连接到对方。这对于整体速度有着非常不利的影响。
对于这个问题，有以下解决方式：对于防火墙，打开用于接收连接的端口（即你在BT客户端中定义的端口）；对于NAT，你需要配置NAT服务器使用Basic NAT方式而不是NAPT（不同的路由有着不同的运行方式。翻阅你的路由文档或客服论坛。你也可以在 PortForward 找到关于此问题的大量信息）。

 为什么我的朋友不能加入？ 
用户数目有所限制（你可以查看“首页->站点数据->上限”）。当达到那个数目时，我们会停止接受新成员。
由于非活跃用户(长期不使用账号的用户)引起账号资源浪费，因此我们将清理该部分用户，为其他想加入用户腾出空间。
关于非活跃用户清理规则，参考 规则 。
 怎样自定义头像？ 
首先，找一个你喜欢的图片，当然了它不能违反我们的 规则 。然后你要找一个存放它的地方，比方说我们自己的 上传器 。出于服务器负载的考虑，我们更希望你将图片上传到别的网站，然后将其URL粘贴到你的 控制面板 的头像URL部分。 
请不要为了仅仅测试头像而发帖。如果一切顺利，你将在你的详情页面看到它。
 数据统计 - 
 最常见的数据未能得到更新的原因 
 服务器过载/未响应。只要尝试着保持会话直到服务器恢复响应(不推荐连续手动刷新，这样会加重服务器负载)。
 你正在使用不稳定的客户端。如果你想要使用测试版或者CVS版本，你需要自己承担由此带来的风险。
 最佳的尝试 
 如果你当前正下载/上传的种子并不在你的用户详情页面中，你可以等一会或者强制进行手动更新。
 确保你正确地关闭了客户端软件，否则Tracker服务器无法收到"event=completed"的信号。
 如果Tracker服务器挂了，不要停止上传。只要在你退出客户端之前服务器恢复工作，所有的数据都会得到正确地更新。
 为什么我正在下载/做种的一个种子会在我的详情页面中被列出多次？ 
如果因为某些原因(比方说死机，客户端失去响应)你的客户端非正常退出并且你又重新打开它，它会被分配到一个全新的Peer ID, 这样它显示为一个全新的种子。而旧的种子将永远不会收到“event=completed”或“event=stopped”的信号，因此将一直被列出直到Tracker清理超时的Peer。 无视了它就可以了，它最后会消失的。
 为什么我已经完成/取消的种子仍然在我的详情页面里？ 
有一些客户端，比如说TorrentStorm和Nova Torrent，在取消或者完成一个任务的时候不能向Tracker服务器正确发送信号。在那样的情况下，Tracker服务器将一直保持等待信号的状态（因此会一直列出种子的状态为做种/下载的状态）直到Tracker清理超时的Peer。无视了它就可以了，它最后会消失的。
 多IP（我可以从不同的电脑登录/下载吗？） 
是的，目前Tracker服务器支持单个用户从任意个数的IP地址同时访问/下载。
然而，对于单种是有限制的。对于每个种子，最多允许3个做种的连接，最多只允许1个下载的连接（这意味着，对于某个种子你一次只能在一个地方下载）。
 发布 - 
 为什么我不能发布种子？

 我需要满足哪些条件才能加入发布小组呢？ 
你所必须满足的条件：
 具有稳定的资源来源
 平均每周资源发布数量不少于5个
你必须确保发布的文件符合以下特征:
 不超过7天之前
 你必须要有做种的能力，或者可以确保至少有效供种24小时。
 你需要有至少达到2MBit的上传带宽。

 为什么我的下载有时候停在99%? 
你所下载到的片段越多，寻找拥有你所缺少的片段的同伴就将变得越困难。这就是为什么有时候在下载即将完成的时候，速度会变得非常慢，甚至完全停止了。只要耐心等候，或早或晚剩下的部分一定能够下载到的。
 "部分哈希验证出错"这条信息是什么意思？ 
BT的客户端会检查它所收到的数据的完整性。如果某一个片段在验证中出错，那么这个片段将被重新下载。偶尔的哈希验证错误是非常常见的现象，不用担心。
有些客户端有屏蔽向你发送错误数据的其他客户端的功能。如果有这个选项，最好打开它。因为这样可以保证如果某个同伴经常向你发送错误的数据时，它将会被屏蔽。
 100MB大小的种子，我怎么下了120MB的东西回来? 
参见哈希验证失败的那个问题。如果你的客户端收到了错误的数据，那么它将会重新下载这一部分，因此总下载量有可能比种子大小略微大一些。确保“屏蔽发送错误数据的客户端”的那个选项被打开了，这样可以减少额外的下载。

IO错误指的是输入-输出错误，这是一个文件系统错误，而非来自我们的Tracker服务器。当你的客户端由于某些原因不能打开种子中未下载完成的文件时，这个错误就会发生。 通常原因是客户端的两个实例同时在运行：当上一次关闭客户端时因为某种原因它没有被真正关闭，从而始终在后台运行。因此文件被锁定，使得新的实例不能打开这个文件。
另外一个不常出现的原因是因为老旧的FAT文件系统。某些系统崩溃可能导致未下载完成的文件损坏，接着就出现了这个错误。运行一次scandisk应该可以解决这个问题。注意，只有当你使用Windows 9X操作系统（只支持FAT文件系统）或者在Windows NT/2000/XP中使用FAT文件系统的时候才比较可能出现这个问题。NTFS文件系统要健壮许多，不太可能出现这样的问题。

密钥系统在BT客户端连接Tracker服务器时起到验证身份的作用。每一个用户都有一个系统随机生成的密钥。当用户下载某个种子文件时，他的私人密钥被添加到种子文件的Tracker服务器URL中。通过这种方式，你可以在家中或者办公室使用不同的IP来做种某个文件。

首先，如果你不是我们的注册用户，将会发生这个错误。其次，有可能你没有在登录状态下从我们的网页里下载种子文件。如果是这两种情况，只要注册一个帐号或者登录后下载种子文件就可以了。
另外，当你注册了一个新用户并且开始第一次下载的时候，或者你刚刚重置了你的密钥时，也可能出现这个错误。原因是系统并非实时检查密钥的改变。如果是因为这个原因，那么就让种子任务等一会儿，最后一定能收到Tracker服务器发回的成功信息。

 如果你的密钥被泄漏，且别的用户正在使用这个密钥（即使用你的帐户）下载文件。在这种情况下，你能在你的详情页面看到你并未下载或上传的种子。
 当你的客户端崩溃，或者你的连接并没有正常被终止。在这样的情况下，就算你已经关闭了你的客户端，你仍然在你的详情页面看到正在上传/下载的记录。通常情况下这些“冗余种子”将在30分钟之内被自动清除，但是如果你马上继续你的下载而服务器又提示“You already are downloading the same torrent”的错误，那么你需要重置你的密钥，然后重新下载种子文件，之后继续下载过程。

DHT必须从你的客户端被禁止。DHT可能导致你的数据被错误地记录，可以视为一种作弊行为。任何使用DHT的用户将因作弊而被系统禁止。

 我该怎样提升下载速度？ - 
 不要马上下载新发布的种子 
下载速度主要取决于上传者/下载者比(SLR)。如果是种子是新发布的且非常受欢迎而SLR又很低的种子，下载速度低是常见的问题。
请牢记你不喜欢低速下载。所以多 上传 让别人不用忍耐同样的困扰。
由其是当你的带宽较窄时，不要马上下载新发布的种子。最好的下载速度通常在一个种子生命周期的一半时出现，此时SLR达到最大值（不过，这时下载的缺点是你的上传量不会很多。究竟如何平衡优点与缺点，取决于你自己)。
 限制上传速度 
上传速度将从以下两种方式显著影响下载速度：
 Bittorrent的同伴倾向于回馈那些给它们提上传的同伴。这就意味着如果A和B正在同时下载一个文件，而A又在高速向B传送数据，那么B将会尝试着回报A。因此高速上传将导致高速下载。
 由于TCP协议的工作方式，当A正从B下载某些东西的时候，A必须不停地向B发送成功收到B所发送来的数据的信号（被称为确认──ACK ── 某种“已收到”的信息)。如果A没有发送ACK信号，那么B将暂停向A发送数据并且进入等候状态。如果A正在全速上传，很有可能没有用来发送ACK信号的带宽，因此ACK信号被耽搁。在这种情况下，过高速度的上传导致了低速的下载。
实际的效果是以上两个原因的结合。上传速度应该在保证ACK能正常传输的前提下被设得尽量高。 一个很好的实践理论是保持上传速度在理论上限的80%。 你也可以细细研究什么是最适合你的速度（同时也请记住高速上传对于你的分享率很有帮助）。
如果你正在运行一个以上的种子任务，你应该考虑的是全局上传速度。某些客户端能限制了全局上传速度，其他的则能对每一个种子分别进行设置。了解你的客户端。如果你正在使用你的电脑做别的某些应用（比方说上网或者从FTP拖东西），也需考虑一下它们对于全局上传的影响。
 限制同时连接数 
某些操作系统（例如Windows 9X）对于大量连接数支持不完善，甚至有可能因此而崩溃。也有一些家用路由（尤其当运行着NAT以及/或者打开防火墙状态检查服务时）会因大量连接数而变得很慢或者崩溃。对于连接数没有固定的最佳值，你可以试试看60或者100。记住这些连接数是累加的，所以如果你的客户端运行了两个会话，这两个数字要加在一起。
 限制同时上传数 
上传数难道和连接数有什么不一样吗？是的，两者是不同的。连接数限制了你的客户端所能对话以及/或者下载的同伴数。上传数则限制了你的客户端实际能上传的同伴数。理想的数值一般要比连接数低许多，并且与你的物理带宽高度相关。
 那怎么办？等待一会吧 
如我们在上面所解释的，在BT下载过程中一个同伴更加倾向于回报那些上传给它的同伴。当你开始一个新的下载任务时，你没有文件片断提高给其他同伴，因此他们通常会无视你。这使得开始阶段的下载非常缓慢，由其是当你所连接到的同伴只有很少是（或者没有）做种者。一旦你获得了一些能用于共享的文件片断，下载速度会有所改观。
 为什么在我下载的时候浏览网页速度如此之慢？ 
你的下载带宽是有限的。如果你正在下载一个速度很快的种子，它几乎肯定将占满你的下载带宽。这是浏览网页显然就会变慢。很多BT客户端允许你限制下载速度，你可以试试。
浏览网页只是作为举例之一，同样的问题也会出现在游戏，即时通信软件上......
 我的网络提供商（ISP）使用了透明代理。我应该怎么做？ - 
 什么是代理？ 
基本上说，代理就是中间人。当你通过代理访问某个站点的时候，你的请求将首先被发送到代理处，然后由代理转发到你所请求的站点，而不是你直接连通到网站。下面是几种典型的代理分类（术语不是那么的规范）：
 透明代理 
 透明代理在客户端无需配置。他将自动把80端口的信息重定向到代理(有时候也作为非匿名代理的同义词)； 
 显式代理 
 浏览器必须经过配置才能使用代理； 
 匿名代理 
 代理将不会把客户标记发送至服务器端 (HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR头标志将不被发送。服务器也因此看不到你的IP)； 
 高度匿名代理 
 代理将不会把客户标记或代理标记发送至服务器端 (HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR和HTTP_VIA and HTTP_PROXY_CONNECTION头标志将不被发送。服务器看不到你的IP，甚至不知道你正在使用代理)； 
 公用 
 (不言自明了)。 
透明代理可能是匿名的，也可能是非匿名的，且匿名也有相应的等级。
 我该怎样发现自己正处于一个（透明的/匿名的）代理后面？ 
试试看 ProxyJudge 。它列出了服务器端从你这里所收到的HTTP的头标志。相关的几个标志是HTTP_CLIENT_IP，HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR和REMOTE_ADDR。
 我的“可连接”是“否”尽管我并没有NAT或者防火墙？ 
Tracker服务器在寻找你的真实IP方面非常有天赋。但是这需要代理发送HTTP头标志HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR。如果你的ISP的代理没有这么做的话，Tracker服务器将把代理的IP当作你的客户端的IP。所以当你登录之后，Tracker服务器尝试连接你的客户端来确信你没有使用NAT/防火墙，服务器实际上将试图连接代理的IP（使用你的BT客户端报告的接收连接端口）。很自然地，代理服务器并没有监听那个端口。如此连接会失败，而Tracker服务器也因此认为你使用了NAT/防火墙。
 为什么我连不上？难道我被网站屏蔽了？ - 
 也许是因为我的IP地址被列入黑名单了？ 
这个网站有屏蔽被禁用户或攻击者的IP地址的功能。该功能在Apache/PHP层面上起作用，且只能屏蔽从这些地址 登录 网站。这不会阻止你 连接 到网站，更无法从底层的协议层面进行屏蔽。即便你的地址已经被列入了黑名单，你应该仍能够通过ping/traceroute命令连同服务器。如果你不能连通服务器，那么问题的原因在别处。
如果你的IP地址因某种原因错误地被我们屏蔽了，请联系我们。
 你的ISP屏蔽了本站的地址 
首先，这一般不像你的ISP的所作所为。DNS域名解析以及/或者网络问题是常见的真凶。
对此我们无能为力。你应该联系你的ISP（或者换一个）。记住你仍然可以通过代理访问本站，参看此常见问题关于代理的部分。在这种情况下，代理是否匿名或者使用哪个监听端口都不重要了。
注意，你的“可连接状态”将因此一直被列为“否”，因为此时Tracker服务器无法检查你的BT客户端接收连接的状态。
 How can I help translate the site language into my native language? - 
 What skills do I need to do the translation? 
Translate the site into another language is quite easy. You needn't be skilled in PHP or dynamic website design. In fact, all you need is proficient understanding of English (the default site language) and the language you plan to translate into. Maybe some basic knowledge in HTML would help.
Moreover, we give a detailed tutorial on how to do the translation HERE . And our coders would be more than pleased to answer the questions you may encounter.
Translate the whole site into another language would take estimated 10 hours. And extra time is needed to maintain the translation when site code is updated.
So, if you think you could help, feel free to CONTACT US . Needless to say, you would be rewarded.
 The translation tutorial 
 How does multi-language work?
Currently we use language files to store all the static words that a user can see on web pages. 
Every php code file has a corresponding language file for a certain language. And we named the language file 'lang_' plus the filename of the php code file. i.e. the language file of the php code file 'details.php' would be 'lang_details.php'.

 What's in language files?

 [[ about_clients ]]
 TorrentLeech.org Wiki 
 Trace: » about_clients 
 Table of Contents
 About Clients 
 What a Client is 
 What happens if I use a client that's causing trouble? 
 Recommended Clients 
 Banned Clients 
 Not Recommended Clients 
 Final Comments 
 About Clients 
 What a Client is 
A torrent client is a piece of software that allows leeching (downloading) and seeding (uploading) of torrents. There are many clients out there, each with their own features and charm, and we encourage users to try several of them to see what tickles their fancy. We won't recommend a specific client, but at the end of this chapter we'll tell you ones which you could try based on functionality, user experience and feedback we've received over the years.
 What happens if I use a client that's causing trouble? 
It's important you pick the correct client, as some are so out of date that they will report malformed stats. The first problem with that is your stats being off on site. Some clients also hammer our hardware, which in turn can affect the performance of it for all users. In most cases you will be contacted by staff first, get a warning or in more severe cases your account will be banned. We suggest you use permitted clients only to keep your account and the site safe and working at its best.
 Recommended Clients 
We have seen a lot of clients come through and the following is a list of those we have seen working best on TL.
 Name License Windows macOS Linux BSD Notes 
 BitTorrent Proprietary, Adware X X 
 Deluge GPL 3 or later X X X X 
 qBittorrent GPL 2 or later X X X 
 rTorrent GPL 2 or later X X Often accompanied by ruTorrent 
 Transmission GPL 2 or GPL 3 X X X X Synology Download Station uses this library. This is also the default BitTorrent client of many Unix and Linux distributions. 
 Banned Clients 
The following clients are banned from Torrentleech
 Thunderbolt (a.k.a Xunlei)
 FOLX download manager
 Freebox BitTorrent
 BiglyBT
 Some versions of μTorrent (mainly older than the 2.2.0 version for Windows)
 Bitcomet
 Tixati
 BitWombat
 Transmission 4.0.6 (Announce bug)
We also do not permit beta clients, or clients which have been forked from major clients and/or altered in some way. Any Debrid service you may use will eventually lead to your account being disabled, we do not allow this kind of traffic.
 Not Recommended Clients 
The following clients are NOT RECOMMENDED at Torrentleech. While they may work, they are not mainstream, not tested or in some other cases just plain unsuitable.
 Name Why not recommended 
 FlashGet No longer maintained 
 Free Download Manager Not really designed to be a torrent client workhorse 
 KGet No longer maintained 
 KTorrent No longer maintained 
 Lftp No longer maintained 
 LimeWire 
 μTorrent for Web Do you seriously want your torrenting activity controlled from the cloud? 
 Miro No longer maintained 
 MLDonkey No longer maintained 
 Opera C'Mon, it's a web browser - not really designed to be a torrent client workhorse 
 Robert No longer maintained 
 Shareaza No longer maintained 
 Tonido No longer maintained 
 Final Comments 
 For seedboxes (both commercial and home-operated) 
rTorrent is by far a favorite due to its massive logging capabilities, small footprint and speed. Another great thing about rTorrent is that with its companion, ruTorrent, you have a new web friendly front-end and the ability to run autodl-irssi - an Auto Downloading solution. The only downside with rTorrent is that it's single threaded and will often times appear to lock up.
If you find rTorrent too annoying due to its single-cpu limitations, you can always try Deluge instead (specifically, Deluge 2 or newer) - another fine option.
 For home users 
For the truly nerdy, we've put together a guide on how to install rtorrent on Windows . Sadly, this solution does not support ruTorrent or autodl-irssi.
For the general everyday user, qBittorrent might be a good choice for you. Easy to use, nag free, and we've even created our very own Windows based auto-downloader 1) that you can use with qBittorrent. A detailed step-by-step guide to automating downloads to work with qBittorrent is available here 2) 
 Mobile / Tablet clients 
Mobile phones and tablets are not designed to be running applications 24/7. While there are some torrent clients that support iOS and Android, we do not recommend torrenting from those clients. Our users are supposed to keep torrents active for a minimum period of time, or to maintain a ratio and doing either of these on a mobile phone or tablet is ill-advised. VIP's, who have no hit & run requirement as well as no ratio requirement (while their VIP is active), can potentially use this clients worry free in emergency situations.

 Basic searching on TorrentLeech 
 Ticking the box 'Exclude inactive torrents' will only return results with at least 1 seeder
 Ticking the box 'Exclude Music and 0-day' will exclude those categories from search results
 Ticking the box 'Search Title only' will only search the torrent title, and not file list or NFO as well
 Adding a dash right before a term searches for everything except that term: Beetlejuice -dv searches for everything Beetlejuice related but excluding 'dv'.
 Adding a dash with the tags: prefix will let you exclude certain tags, example: lord of the rings -tags:FREELEECH or lord of the rings -tags:FREELEECH,Drama,nonscene 
 Advanced searching on TorrentLeech 
 IMDB searching 
You can search IMDB ID to quickly find all releases of a single IMDB movie or series. Input the IMDB ID including the 'tt'-prefix. So if you want to find all Rocky II releases, input only tt0084602 in the searchbar.
 Anime (Anilist) 
You can search Anilist ID to quickly find all releases of a single Anilist anime. To use this function you will need to use a prefix in the search: anilistID , followed by a colon, then the ID. Example: anilistID:1818 .

 Part seeding for uTorrent 
A very good way to improve your ratio is part seeding. 
What does it mean? The name gives a good hint - you seed only a part of a torrent (a few .rar files)
Why? Downloading only a part of big torrent dont hurt your ratio, but everyone who downloads the whole torrent, will be downloading the part you seed and it's a lot easier to seed it to 1.0 or more ratio.
How? This guide will show you how to part seed with uTorrent.
IMPORTANT NOTE: this will NOT work if you have wait time on the torrent.
Also do not try to part seed PACK's, because the “leechers” you see on the torrent are already actually part seeders.
First, select a torrent to part seed. In this example we use “Need for Speed Hot Pursuit-RELOADED”
If you are a new user with wait times, you must download the torrent from browse page, not the torrent details page.
Click the “Download torrent” button. Select “Open” or “Open with: uTorrent” in the download box that appears.
Now the “Add new torrent” window appears in utorrent. As we dont want to downlaod all files, click “Select none” button:
Select some random .rar files there. 3-4 files will be enough.
Once you have selected the parts you want click on ok. Utorrent will then begin to download those parts you have selected. Once downloaded, sit back, relax and watch your ratio grow 
You have now successfully achieved Part Seeding in uTorrent. Congratulations!

autobrr [TorrentLeech.org Wiki]
 [[ autobrr ]]
 TorrentLeech.org Wiki 
 Trace: » autobrr 
 Table of Contents
 What is autobrr? 
 Installing autobrr 
 Enable RSS 
 Initial Configuration 
 Configure your Client 
 Configure Filters 
 Configure the IRC Network 
 Check for Releases 
 Troubleshooting Issues 
 Is your bot on IRC? 
 Is your bot seeing announces? 
 What is autobrr? 
Autobrr is the next generation of automated download systems which can help you build your ratio or automatically grab specific torrents for topics that interest you. It is similar to autodl-irssi except you're not forced to use rTorrent, and it is much more user friendly to configure. Autobrr idles on an IRC server and automatically downloads torrents when they are announced. This allows users to grab releases as soon as they become available to maximize seed time. In comparison it is much faster than RSS and will usually yield the best seeding results.
 Installing autobrr 
Because there are so many different seedbox configurations and ways to install the software, this guide will not cover the steps to install it. If you are using a seedbox from a well-known provider, chances are you can install it directly from your box's control panel. Otherwise, head over to their install guide and choose your preferred method. Come back to this guide once it's installed and accessible.
 Enable RSS 
autobrr uses your RSS key to download the torrent from the site to ensure the file it grabs is linked to your user. You'll need to enable RSS access in your profile if not already on, follow this guide for more information..
 Initial Configuration 
After installing, you can access the web interface from http: <local.ip.add.ress>:7474 
===== Set a Password =====
Once at the web interface, you will need to choose a username and strong password, save that, and log in.
===== Configure the Indexer =====
Navigate to the top menu, then Settings, then Indexers, then click + Add new indexer.
In the Indexer dropdown, scroll down to the bottom and select TorrentLeech.
If accessing the main TorrentLeech.org site is blocked by your ISP , you can change the Base URL to one of our mirror sites to allow your bot to download the releases.
Shouldn't be an issue for most seedbox providers.
In the RSS key field, fill in the RSS key from your profile. Do not enter the entire URL , only the part after rss.torrentleech.org. 
See the above mentioned Enable RSS section if you need help locating your RSS key. Also ensure you are only using your RSS key, your passkey or IRC key will not work here.
Your key should look like the below screenshot, if there are any parts of the URL in this field it is wrong. 
Under the IRC section, enter nickname_bot for the Nick, where nickname is your Torrentleech username. Leave the NickServ Account and Password blank, bot nicks do not need to be registered.
Once all configuration is done, your sidebar should look like the below. Click Save to submit your changes.
 Configure your Client 
Click Clients on the left-hand side, then click + Add new client. Enter a name, then select your client from the list. 
For most seedboxes this will either be rTorrent or qBittorrent. Fill in the requested information for your client. In this example I am using rTorrent, so the Host would be https://my.domain.name/RPC2 .
If you have a username and password set on your rTorrent, it will need to be added into this field as well. Contact your seedbox provider if unsure. 
Click Test to make sure autobrr can properly communicate with your client, and then click Create. If you get stuck, autobrr has documentation on configuring it for use on a shared seedbox .
 Configure Filters 
Filters are what tell autobrr which files you want to download. These could be used to download only a specific category of torrent, specific episodes of a TV show, or only torrents marked as freeleech. If you do not configure any filters, autobrr will not download any releases. In this example, I will set autobrr to download any freeleech torrent which is announced. Click Filters in the top menu, then click Add new. Give it a name, then click Create. Click the ”…” next to the new filter and click Edit. Next to the Filter Name, select TorrentLeech from the Indexers dropdown, and turn on the Enabled toggle at the bottom of the page. It is also recommended to set the Delay to a minimum of 5 seconds, as this will ensure that the download link is live on the site and doesn't return an error when trying to snatch the release. If you want to specify a minimum or maximum size, set limits on the max number of downloads per hour, day, etc, you can do so on this page as well.
Next, go to the Advanced tab. Scroll to the bottom and enable the Freeleech toggle. Do not fill in the Freeleech Percent box, as TL does not use partial freeleech systems. 
Scroll back up and click the Actions tab. Click Add new, set the Type to the download client you configured in the previous section, and give the action a name. Once you select a type, additional options will appear. At a minimum, you need to also select the Client from the dropdown that appears below Type. If you want to specify additional settings like a torrent label or a custom save path, you can also do so from this page. Click Save in the lower right.
 Configure the IRC Network 
Once you add the Indexer, autobrr should automatically configure the IRC network settings. All you need to do is enable the network so your bot joins the channel. Click Settings at the top again, then select IRC on the left. Click the “Enabled” slider next to TorrentLeech. The network will highlight in red for several seconds while autobrr connects to the network and joins the channel, then the highlight should disappear and a green dot will appear next to the network.
 Check for Releases 
After following all of the previous steps, your autobrr client should be joined into the announces channel and watching for new releases to hit the site. To confirm this, select the Releases tab up top. Be patient as there are sometimes long gaps between releases that match your filter. Once a release has been announced that matches your filters, it will appear on this page. A green check next to the torrent name means it successfully executed the action configured for the filter (such as sending to rTorrent).
If you see a red exclamation point, click on it to determine why that particular release failed to push.
 Troubleshooting Issues 
If it has been 30+ minutes and you still don't see any Releases appearing, there is likely an issue with your setup.
 Is your bot on IRC? 
Join our IRC server ( guide ) and, once connected, use the following command: 
 /whois your_bot_name_here
You will get a response telling you whether your bot is in any channels, and if so in which channels. Your bot should be in only one channel: #tlannounces. Your bot should never join our main channel #torrentleech.
If you bot is not in #tlannounces then you probably have an error in your setup. Use our guide to check your settings step by step.
 Is your bot seeing announces? 
Open the Logs tab in autobrr and leave it open for a few minutes. autobrr does not pull any old logs into this view, only new ones that have been generated since you opened the page. For each announce to the site, autobrr should log a couple lines for it. As you can see in the below example, autobrr rejected this release because it isn't a freeleech torrent. Examine your filter settings to ensure everything is set properly.

autodl.irssi [TorrentLeech.org Wiki]
 [[ autodl.irssi ]]
 TorrentLeech.org Wiki 
 Trace: » autodl.irssi 
 Table of Contents
 Quick details 
 What is autodl-irssi? 
 Configuration of autodl-irssi for use with Torrentleech 
 Enable RSS 
 Configure autodl-irssi with your Torrentleech RSS key 
 Configure the IRC Server settings 
 Configuring Filters on your Seedbox 
 Important: Disable output to channel 
 How to troubleshoot autodl-irssi issues 
 Is your bot on IRC? 
 Is your bot seeing the announces? 
 I`m getting a Freeleech error on those torrents 
 Quick details 
 Server: irc.torrentleech.org
 Port: 7011 or +7021 ( SSL )
 Channel: #tlannounces
 You do not need a key to join the announce channel
 Bots do not go into any other channels
 What is autodl-irssi? 
Autodl-irssi is a plugin for the web-based clients, where rutorrent is the preferred option. Autodl-irssi allows users to configure an IRC client (irssi) to idle on an IRC server and automatically download torrents when they are announced. This allows users to grab releases as soon as they become available to maximise seed time. In comparison it is much faster than RSS and will usually yield the best seeding results.
 Configuration of autodl-irssi for use with Torrentleech 
We assume that autodl-irssi is already installed and properly configured. If this is not the case then you should contact your provider if they can assist you with the installation of the plugin.
 Enable RSS 
First you need to enable your RSS access, if you haven't done so already. Need help? Follow this guide .
 Configure autodl-irssi with your Torrentleech RSS key 
Once you have enabled RSS , you need to enter the RSS key shown in to autodl-irssi. To do this, login to your web based torrent client, click on the autodl-irssi configuration icon and select “Trackers”: 
Select Torrentleech from the list shown, and paste the RSS key shown within your Torrentleech
profile (similar to that in Figure 3 ), and set the “ Delay ” field to 5: 
Note that if copying/pasting the full http: link into the box in Figure 5 , it will automatically shorten the URL to include just the RSS Key. We now need to configure a “ Watch Folder ”, which is a folder that Autodl-Irssi saves the .torrent files to once they are announced. Click OK to save the RSS settings and click the Autodl-Irssi icon once again. This time you need to click on the Preferences option.
Navigate to the “Action” tab, and then specify a directory on your Seedbox slot that you have write
permissions. ( The /torrents/watch folder is the default watch folder):
Click OK to save the new settings and continue with the next step.
 Configure the IRC Server settings 
click the Autodl-Irssi icon once again and select “IRC Servers” from the autodl-irssi configuration icon: 
This is the section of the program where we configure the IRC server that autodl-irssi will connect
to.
Click on the “New” button located at the bottom left of this box, and then specify the following
details..
 Server - irc.torrentleech.org 
 Port: - 7011 
 Nick: - nickname_bot (where nickname is your Torrentleech username)
Click on the “New” button located under the IRC Channel section of this box, and enter
 Channel: #tlannounces 
Note that should you wish to use SSL , change the port to 7021 and tick the “SSL” box, however we
recommend using a standard connection during the initial configuration so that you don't have to troubleshoot SSL should anything go wrong for you.
Click on the “ OK” button, and the Seedbox will then connect to the Torrentleech IRC server, this is
verified by the Autodl-Irssi logs & by doing a /whois botnickname whilst on the IRC server:
Now that we have the bot connected to the server in the Announces channel, we now need to
configure filters to tell the bot what torrent files to grab.
 Configuring Filters on your Seedbox 
The way that autodl filters work is that you specify keywords for the releases you would like it to match and download/seed. 
Shouldyou wish to match multiple words, you needseparate them using the “*” symbol, for example, to match
the release for “How I Met Your Mother” , you specify the filter “How*I*Met*Your*Mother” .
Click the Autodl-Irssi configuration icon and click on “Filters”:
The Filters options will then appear:
These options are as follows:
 Display name: This is the name of the filter and should be something meaningful so you can identify what this filter is for, we will use “How I Met Your Mother” here,
 Match releases: This is the match syntax, so to match “How I Met Your Mother” , we enter “How*I*Met*Your*Mother” 
 Except releases: Enter any exceptions to these releases, for example if you don’t want 720p releases then enter “720p” in this box
 Match sites: Click this button and select “Torrentleech” from the list of trackers in the list:
 Minimum Size: Enter a minimum size release should you require it (i.e 100mb)
 Maximum Size: Enter a maximum size should it be required (i.e 900mb)
You can also specify a maximum number of downloads per day/week/month , this is self explanatory.
Once the desired fields have been entered, click OK and the filter will be applied meaning your bot
will then automatically download any torrents that meet the specified filter criteria.
The filter shown above will automatically download any “How I Met Your Mother” release from Torrentleech, that are larger than 100mb, but smaller than 900mb. The filter limits to 2 downloads per week, and excludes 720p releases.

 Is your bot on IRC? 
Join our IRC server ( guide ) and, once connected, use the following command:

You will get a response telling you whether your bot is in any channels, and if so in which channels. Your bot should be in only one channel: #tlannounces. Your bot should never join our main channel #torrentleech.

 Being Connectable 
 How peering works 
Before we explain what it means to be connectable, it's important for us to understand how peering works.
When you start a torrent, your client sends a notification to the tracker that you are opting to be a peer for this torrent. Your client also tells the tracker what Port number your torrent client is configured to listen on. This process is known as an “Announce”. The tracker will respond to your announcement, and will provide you a list of other peers which contains a dictionary of IP Addresses and port numbers of other peers. The list will contain up to 50 IP addresses of other peers.
After your torrent client has received this list of peers, it will attempt to contact each one (dependent on any limitations set in your client), and request chunks of data. If the other party has data that it can share with you, they reply saying that they are interested. You then negotiate which chunks you would like to get, and then your client requests those chunks. Once your client has downloaded a full chunk of data (correctly known as a “piece”), then it makes that piece available to other peers.
All these peers are collectively called a swarm, and whenever you start your torrent, you are joining the swarm.
 Leeching and seeding 
In order for you to be able to establish an outbound connection to another peer, that peer needs to be “connectable”. An outbound connection could be either:
 You requesting a piece (you leeching, them seeding)
 You offering a piece (you seeding, them leeching)
In order for another peer to be able to establish an inbound connection to you, you need to be “connectable”. An inbound connection could be either:
 Them requesting a piece (them leeching, you seeding)
 Them offering a piece (them seeding, you leeching)
 If both peers are not “connectable”, then neither of you will be able to peer with the other, meaning you have just lost the ability to speak to that peer in the swarm. When this happens, you lose the opportunity to leech and/or seed to this peer. You're probably thinking “ah, well, not a problem, that's just 1 peer, there's 49 other healthy peers”. Well, you'd be dead wrong. The only kinds of peers which are pretty much guaranteed to always be connectable are seedboxes, and generally speaking they will have lots to share with you, but you will have nothing to share back to them. Remember the saying - every little bit helps!
 Timing is a factor 
Assuming you are content with being not “connectable” - and rely on others being connectable. What does this mean? Let's assume for a moment that you were the very first person to join the swarm. You are peer number 1. When peer number 2 joins, he learns about you - but you do not learn about him until your next announce, which is usually 30 minutes later. If peer 2 can't connect to you, he then has to sit and wait until Peer 3 comes along. Peer 3 will learn about Peer 1 (you) and peer 2, and let's assume that Peer 3 is the only one with actual content (it was the uploader). Peer 3 will try to connect to Peer 1 and 2, and if Peer 2 is “connectable”, then Peer 3 sends all of its pieces to Peer 2. All the while this happens, you are sitting there, completely left out. After your half hour timer is up, and you send a new announce, you learn about peer 2 and 3, and can connect to both to receive data. But since both already have the entire content completely, you've lost out on seeding.
The initial swarm is the best time to get seeding opportunity - it's the most active time of a torrent, and the best time to gain upload credit for sharing. After the initial swarm, seeding opportunity declines dramatically, and now you have to seed for ages just to be able to have the possibility to recoup your ratio. Remember, we require non VIP's to seed 1:1 on every torrent - or for a length of time, whichever comes first - or it will be considered hit & run and could penalize you in the end.
 Being "connectable" 
Essentially, what it means to be “connectable” is that a peer is able to connect to your torrent client port at your publicly visible IP Address. There are two protocols that can be used - TCP and uTP (which is a transport protocol on top of UDP). A long time ago, our computers were connected to the Internet using modems, meaning that those computers got their own publicly accessible IP Address. All that was then needed was for the firewall (assuming you had one) to allow the application to accept connections on whatever port it desired, or alternatively, you allowed only the port numbers you wanted the torrent client to use.
These days, it's a bit more complicated because almost everybody will have a box called a router, which allows multiple devices to access the internet using a technology known as NAT (Network Address Translation). In this case, you have to rely on something called port forwarding to allow yourself to become connected.
 How to check if I'm "connectable"? 
Before you start making any changes, first check if you are connectable. Open your torrent client, and find out which port it is listening on. I can't share images for every client, but here's an example of qBitTorrent.
Go to a website named CanYouSeeMe and it will already know what your public facing IP address is, all you have to do is furnish it with the port number and click “Check Port” If all is well, you should see a message like this:
All is well! You don't have to do anything else, since you are connectable!
If you get this kind of message:
Then you have some more work to do. Continue reading!
 How to become "Connectable" 
 Option 1 - Hope and Pray that UPnP works 
In the image above you may have noticed this checkbox:
Turn this on, and then completely restart your torrent client. With qBittorrent, you should quit it completely (CTRL+Q) and restart. After this, run the CanYouSeeMe test above.
UPnP is Universal Plug and Play. It is a set of networking protocols that permits networked devices, such as personal computers, printers, Internet gateways, Wi-Fi access points and mobile devices to seamlessly discover each other's presence on the network and establish functional network services. This is by far the simplest solution, provided your router supports UPnP.
If you are still unsuccessful, try the next option.
 Option 2 - Port Forward 
Essentially what you want to do is forward the port number (in my case, 63041) from your routers WAN interface to your computer's internal IP address. Due to the vast amount of different routers there are out there, I can't explain to you how this is done, but thankfully a site exists which gives you detailed step-by-step instructions on how to perform a port forwarding. You should find your computer's IP address - you can do this by typing “IPCONFIG” in a command prompt.
It's not likely that this IP address will change, but it is possible, so if you find that the port forward stops, then change the port forward on your router. 
After you have your internal IP address, and your port number to hand, head on over to Port Forward - All Routers , find your model of router and follow the guide. When it asks if you want TCP, UDP or Both, use Both. Sometimes it will show as TCP/UDP, in which case this is the right one to use. If you can only select one OR the other, then TCP is the safest bet!
Once you have set up port forwarding, do the test above to see if the port is open.
 Further Troubleshooting 
If you are absolutely positively sure that the port forwarding has been set up on your router, and you are still not “connectable”, then try these troubleshooting steps:
 Ensure that your bittorrent client is listening on your LAN interface on the port number you have selected. You can use netstat -nato | findstr <port number> 
 like this:
 Ensure that you have configured your bittorrent client to create an exception in the Windows Firewall (if it supports this automatically)
 Manually add your bittorrent application to your firewall rules. Here's an example:
 Restart your torrent client. If you've just added new rules, they won't take effect until you re-start the client.
 Temporarily disable your firewall, then run the test. If it still fails, then double and triple check your port forwarding!
 VPN 
Unfortunately, many of us are forced to use VPN's due to our silly governments or even our ISP 's trying to reduce our fun. This also complicates matters, because many VPN providers support port forwarding, and many VPN providers do not. Check with your VPN provider to see if they do port forwarding. Those that do will generally support custom port options, or use port numbers which are calculated mathematically. Refer to your VPN providers support page, or VPN application to see which port has been forwarded to you, and then configure your torrent client to use that port. Remember to always re-start your torrent client when your port number is changed - some applications support changing port numbers on the fly, and some do not.
 PrivateVPN 
If you are using our affiliate vendor, PrivateVPN, you can see which port is forwarded by going Advanced view and seeing the port there. Make your Torrent client use that same port number, and then restart your torrent client.
To learn more about PrivateVPN, and to make use of our affiliate VIP offer, visit our information page at PrivateVPN . Please note that the VIP offer is only valid once per account.
 CG:NAT users 
We have several users who no longer get a publicly accessible IP Address, due to insufficient number of IPv4 Addresses in the world. These users get IPv6 IP Addresses (which our tracker does not fully support yet), as well as private IPv4 IP Addresses. This technology is known as Circuit Grade Network Address Translation. It's therefore impossible to get an IPv4 forwarded from the outside in.
Until we get proper IPv6 support in our tracker database, please consider using a VPN like the one we recommend, as through the VPN you will be able to get a port forwarded in to you.
 Forcing IPv4 peer Announce 
At the time of writing, we do not fully support IPv6. While the web site and tracker are accessible via IPv6, the tracker database does not support IPv6 addresses. If you have IPv6, it is recommended to force your BitTorrent client to announce your public IPv4 IP Address.
Without doing this, you will be only able to connect to IPv4 peers, and they will not be able to connect to you, a similar problem with being not “connectable”. By doing this suggestion, you have a chance to be included in the pool of peers sent to other peers when they announce.
Tip: To find your public IPv4 Address, visit I Can Haz IP (v4) 
 qBittorrent 
For qBitTorrent, 
 Go to Options
 Click on Advanced
 Scroll All the way to the bottom
 Enter in your publicly accessible IP address
 Restart
 Conclusion 
We hope that you have found this article informative, and that you take being connectable seriously. We cannot guarantee that you will magically get higher upload speed, but we can guarantee that you have significantly increased your chances to peer with almost all peers.

 Warnings 
There are two types of warnings:
 System warning: the site automatically warns you, usually related to your ratio.
 Manual warning: a moderator has warned you manually, be very careful with how you proceed.
 Have you been warned by the system for your ratio? 
We require our users to keep a global ratio of 0.4. That means the moment you go below that threshold, the system will issue a warning to your account. From the moment that happens, you have 7 days to up your ratio to 0.4 or above. The system will automatically check your ratio again after 7 days. If you are at 0.4 or above by then, the warning will be removed and you can continue using TorrentLeech like before (but with a better ratio…). If you do not meet the required ratio your account will be disabled.
If you believe that you should be granted more time to fix your ratio, you can join our IRC channel #tlhelp and explain why. On a case to case basis our moderators will then decide whether to grant you an extension or not.
 Have you been warned by a moderator? 
You have been a bad, bad member. A moderator has issued you a warning. That can be related to your behaviour, it could be a hit and run , a torrent comment or a forum post you have made. If it is unclear to you why you have been issued a warning then come talk to us on IRC .

 FreeLeech on TorrentLeech 
If we look back for the past 15 years, we think the MOST ever requested feature on site was Freeleech. To be fair, it’s more challenging and difficult than it sounds! Its not as simple as press a button to make everything Freeleech. We have observed lots of private trackers over the years that they implemented the Freeleech idea, but in the end it was doing more bad than good. Reason? Because most people get the FREE part of the Freeleech and they think”oh well, its free so why to seed it back?”.
That was our challenge also.
After lots of tests and thoughts and redesigns and calculations, we believe that we finally found a way to overcome this problem, and make Freeleech viable on TL as well! We put several checks in place to make sure that everyone plays fair, with the main concern untouched : MAKE SURE EVERYTHING IS PROPERLY SEEDED for the years to come! Enough talking though, lets go straight to the point :slight_smile:
As you most probably already noticed, there is a new tag in lot of torrents, named FREELEECH plus a Freeleech tag :slight_smile: So what really changed?
 What exactly does FreeLeech mean? 
Freeleech on TL means that download a torrent tagged as FreeLeech will not count towards your downloaded data amount. So if you download a torrent your ratio will not be negatively affected. Seeding, however, will accrue the normal amount of data (so upload 1GB get 1GB added to your upload).
 How do I know which torrents are FreeLeech? 
FreeLeech torrents are marked with a special FreeLeech tag: 
 All boxsets and packs will be marked FreeLeech
 Any torrent above 14GB will be FreeLeech, regardless of category
You need to be in V5 (latest version) in order to see the FreeLeech tags. Torrents that are FreeLeech remain freeleech on older versions of course, but you won't be able to distinguish them.
 What's the catch? 
ALL torrents including FreeLeech are required to be seeded to a 1:1 ratio OR for the required amount of hours for your user class ! Failing to do so will charge you with 1(one) Hit and Run torrent, read more about our Hit and Run system here .

 Outside seeding using Vuze/Azureus 
 Outside seeding is when instead of downloading the files from Torrentleech you instead download the files from another source and then use them to seed the Torrent on Torrentleech .
New users get the most out of outside seeding as it gives a boost to a users upload without havingto download any files thus increasing their ratio quickly.
For this example I will be using [HorribleSubs] Naruto Shippuuden ‐ 189 [720p].mkv however thiswill work with any other release as long as the files are exactly the same, when I say exactly the same I mean 100% matching This is because the hashcheck must be the same on your files obtained elsewhere and the files listed on the site.
 Step 1 
First find a torrent on a public or another private tracker that you think you might be able to find on Torrentleech . While looking I found the torrent [HorribleSubs] Naruto Shippuuden ‐ 189 [720p].mkv .
 Step 2 
Try to locate that torrent in Torrentleech this may not always be possible but in this case I found the exact same torrent here. Now that you have found it on Torrentleech download it from the public/other private torrent site you found it in the Step 1.
 Step 3 
Wait till the torrent has finished when it has finished stop the torrent.
 Step 4 
Download the .torrent file from Torrentleech you found in step 2 and in Vuze click on File‐> Open ‐> Torrent File.. or Ctrl + O.
 Step 5 
Click Add Files and Navigate to the file you downloaded in Step 2 and open it. You can also drag and drop the .torrent file in if you know what you are doing.
 Step 6 
Change Add Mode to Stopped, also make sure the Location to save data: matches the location of the files downloaded in Step 1. Once this is done Click OK
 Step 7 
You will be presented with the following window, Hit OK. If you do not see this window you have done something wrong. Generally this will be the file paths or names don’t match.
 Step 8 
Navigate to Library ‐> Downloading. Right click on the torrent and hit force recheck. 
Your torrent should now look something like this:
Checking can take quite a while depending on the size of the torrent. In this case it will only take a few seconds.
 Step 9 
Once the recheck is done if all the files matched your torrent should have been moved toLibrary ‐> Unwatched if so go to Step 9.
If the file is still in downloading area this means that the torrent had files that didn’t match. Go to Step 9b. 
 Step 9b 
You have two choices now. You can download the parts that are missing from Torrentleech in which case go to step 9, or you can disable the files from downloading. To stop files from downloading right click on the torrent and click show details.
Next click on Files. After this right click on the files that didn’t match and go to Set Priority ‐> Do not download. Once this is done the file should be moved into the unwatched section.
 Step 10 
Start the torrent. You have now successfully completed the guide :D.
 What if the NFO doesn't match? 
Sometimes other places will slightly alter their torrent data including the NFO file and it may be necessary to change it back so that it matches the one on Torrentleech . If you don't do this then your torrent will NOT hashcheck to 100% which is essential in order to start seeding for you. 
Vuze will overwrite the .NFO data to match the one on the site without you having to do anything.
If the torrent does not start seeding because it is stuck on 99.9% (Or similar) then there is usually an issue with the included .NFO file you are trying to match. If you look into the details of the torrent you will find the .NFO file and in most cases where it doesn't hashcheck to 100%, this is usually the cause.

Now press the “Switch to Text” button, the image will change to this:

When you have changed the NFO into text, start from the top left and copy the entire NFO down to the bottom. Doing so ensures that the data will match when you save your newly ammended NFO file.
Using the example NFO shown previously, it should highlight and show as follows:
As you can see we have highlighted “blank data” as well as the text data. This is essential to ensure it will be exactly the same as yours when you save it.

If you just grab a torrent (hit) and then just delete it (run) the system would eventually fall apart. There are two ways for you to give back to the community:
 Seed a torrent to at least 1:1 ratio
 Seed a torrent for at least the minimum time required for your class in total. Be aware that seeding time only counts for fully completed torrents (downloaded 100%). 
Not following this rule will trigger a reminder and eventually an account warning, which in turn can lead to your account being disabled. Read more about these below.
 How long do I have to seed a torrent? 
The time you have to seed a torrent for varies per user class. The so called seeding time only goes into effect on torrents you have downloaded fully. Partially downloaded torrents will never accrue seeding time and need to be seeded 1:1.
 User class Minimum seeding time 
 Registered 10 days 
 Power User 8 days 
 Super User 7 days 
 Extreme User 6 days 
 TL God 4 days 
 VIP User No minimum seeding time 
 How does the system work? 
For every torrent you stop seeding that is either not on a 1:1 ratio or has not been seeded for the minimum time required, you will receive 1 Hit and Run reminder on your account. The reminder will stay visible (and will count to your total amount of hit and runs) as long as you have the torrent inactive. If you have a total of 50 hit and runs on your account for more than 5 consecutive days you will receive a Hit and Run account warning .
The difference between the reminder and account warning is simple: the reminder can be cleared instantly once you start seeding these torrents. Account warnings will be removed after 1 month of good behaviour, as long as there are no new infractions that yield another account warning. If this is the case you can get up to a maximum of 3 account warnings before your account is disabled.
 Warning timeline overview 
 If you stop seeding 50+ low ratio torrents for more than 5 days: The system flags the account and 1st warning is sent and the account is given one (1) month to correct the HnR/ seeding issues.
 If you stop seeding 50+ low ratio torrents for more than 5 days after this month: The system flags the account and 2nd warning is sent and the account is given one (1) month to correct the HnR/ seeding issues.
 If you stop seeding 50+ low ratio torrents for more than 5 days after this month: The system flags the account and 3rd warning is sent and the account will be disabled.
After each account warning you are immune from any further account warnings for the duration of one month to give you chance to correct your HnR/ seeding issues. 
If it has been one (1) month since your last HnR warning then the system will remove 1 HnR warning from your account.
 Where can I find my HnR torrents? 
You can find them on your profile in the 'Hit and Runs' tab.
 How to clear Hit and Runs 
A regular Hit and Run can be easily cleared by seeding the torrent until you have either reached a ratio of 1:1, or until you have seeded for the minimum time required for your user class (see above). Alternatively you can use the HnR tab on your profile page to either use your TL Points or your Surplus Upload Credit (basically your ratio above 1.0) to clear a HnR. You can clear as much HnR as your points or your ratio allow you to, but once your surplus ratio is depleted you can only use TL Points. If those are depleted as well your only option is to start seeding your HnR torrents again.
 How do I know if I can stop seeding? 
You can use the snatchlist tab on your profile to see if torrents are seeded for either the time required or 1:1 ratio.
 Hit and Run FAQ 
 Am I immune from HNR if I donate for VIP? 
Any HnR’s on your account would be wiped and cleared when you get/have VIP. All current & previous HnR warnings will be permanently removed from your account history. (HnR counter would be reset to zero also) Once the VIP period is over you will once again be subject to the HnR policy. Torrents that you have downloaded during your VIP period will not gain HnR after your VIP expires, even if you do not meet the criteria for your new class.
 It says I have torrents that require seeding even though they are seeding? 
Make sure your torrents are loaded and ACTIVE in your torrent client!
 I can see a “torrent requires seeding” link but when I click on it there is nothing there? 
If you just cleared a torrent it may take few seconds for the system to refresh the DB. Give it a few seconds and it would be fine.
 There seems to be a difference between my client stats and the stats on my HNR list? 
Please remember that the tracker is around 30 minutes behind your client as this is how often the tracker updates your stats.
 I have slow upload speeds, will this result in all my torrents being on the HNR list? 
No, it is the amount of torrents you download that will have a bearing on how many torrents you have on your list. You should only download what you can effectively upload back. If this means limiting how much you download to improve your ability to seed back then that is what you must do. An alternative solution would be to get a seedbox 3
 I have limited storage space so cannot seed my torrents back indefinitely? 
You should limit your download activity to match your ability to upload those torrents back. it is no good to keep downloading torrents if you do not have enough storage space to keep them there until you have fully seeded them back. If you do not want to limit your download activity then you will have to invest in extra storage space, a seedbox 3 or a VIP plan 2
 Do I have to seed FreeLeech torrents back? 
Yes, every torrent you download from TL including freeleech is expected to be seeded back fully! Freeleech means your download doesn't count, so its a great way to build your surplus, but that doesn't mean you still don't have to seed it 1:1 or for a minimum time required for your class!
 Torrent files and HnR 
 What can I do to help me seed my files back? 
You should try to download torrents within a few hrs(if no minutes) of being uploaded, and check the peer information on each torrent so that you know if you have a good chance of seeding those torrents back(high seeder/low leecher torrents usually are harder to seed back). Limit the amount of old torrents you download as these are usually the hardest to seed back. Finally, just invest in a seedbox 3
 I removed a torrent from my client when it reached a ratio of 1:1, it then appeared in my HNR list…why? 
If you think one of your torrents has reached a ratio of 1:1 you should first pause it in your client and then wait a minimum of 60 minutes to give the tracker time to update. If the torrent does not appear in your list after this time period you know it is safe to remove the torrent from your client. If it does appear in your HNR list it will tell you how much more you need to seed back before you can remove it from your client. Always check your torrents in this way as it is the tracker ratio on that torrent that counts, not your client ratio. -Alternatively you can make sure that the tracker has updated by also pausing a torrent that you know has a ratio below 1:1 as well as the other torrent you want to check. Only when the tracker has updated will you see the torrent with a ratio below 1:1 on your seeding list. If the original torrent that you were checking has not appeared on the seeding list you will know for sure that it is safe to remove.
 Why did a torrent that I “cleared” reappear in my HNR list shortly afterwards? 
Any torrent you wish to “clear” must be removed from your client first otherwise it will appear back in your list afterwards.
 Why is a torrent that I only partially downloaded showing in my HNR list? 
Every torrent of which you have downloaded at least 10% will appear in your HNR list when you pause or stop seeding them before they reach a ratio of 1:1. Partial downloads never accrue seeding time, so your only option is to seed the data you've downloaded back to a 1:1 ratio. For example if you downloaded 25GB of a 100GB torrent but only seed back 5GB then you will have to clear the remaining 20GB by seeding (or removing it with TL point).
 I've received a HnR warning but there isn’t any torrents in my required seeding list? 
Please remember: If you have been away and received a HnR warning stating you had [x] HnR’s, when you turn your pc back on and log into your TL account your HnR’s will no longer be in your required seeding list as your client would have started seeding again and updated with the TL tracker.

Example: Changing DNS server settings on Windows 7
 Go to the Control Panel.

 So you want to know how to avoid a Warning or ban on Torrent Comments? 
 Introduction 
Comments are a feature of Torrents, and are intended for people to share constructive criticism or feedback regarding the release in question. The provider of the release is notified about each comment, so that they can take necessary action to remediate or correct any problems the release might have.
Comments are also community-driven, meaning that people can contribute to the release by example, providing a description of the release, or perhaps screenshot previews of the release.
It is not meant for:
 Showing gratitude (thanks) - that's what the “Thank You” button is for.
 Spam
 Voicing your opinion about the upload. For example, if you agree with the contents of the upload.
Please keep in mind that Torrentleech offers content to its members. It's up to you wether you download a torrent or not.
Torrentleech does not take sides.
 Guidelines 
 Be polite, trying to look like a badass just makes you look like an idiot.
 Don't flame. Go to 4chan for that.
 If you have something constructive to say about the quality of a release state your case politely.
 Screenshots are always welcome.
 Don't fuel an already lit fire. You may not have caused it but your participation in it can result in a warning as well.
 If you think to yourself “Does my comment add value to this release”, and the answer is no, then you probably should not be posting it.

 What to do if your NFO files doesn't check to 100%? 
If you want to (re)seed a torrent but the NFO doesn't match and you are unable to redownload it from the site for some reason, you can try to manually fix this.
First off: If there is a seed already I just let it re-download. 
If there is no seed and you're trying to reseed a torrent and have all the files and only the NFO or SFV (+ adjacent files) don’t check to 100%, then you can try to redo the line endings in the NFO.
The reason adjacent files are affected is because torrents are transferred in pieces, a piece size can be anything from 1 Byte to 16 MB (it can be larger but older clients like uTorrent 2.2.1 only handle up to 16 MB ). If anything within a piece isn’t 100% perfect the whole piece fails so even when an NFO file of 3 kb doesn’t match you may need to re-download 16 MB to fix it even if the rest of it was perfect.
 Why do you need to poke at line endings? 
Text file lines are terminated differently in Windows/DOS platforms than they are in *nix platforms.
 Unix/Linux platforms terminate a line with LF or 0x0A or ASCII 10
Windows terminates a line with CRLF or 0x0D+0x0A or ASCII 13 + ASCII 10 
If you’ve ever used an old manual typewriter think of LF (Line Feed) as scrolling the paper up to the space under the text you've just typed, and CR (Carriage Return) as moving the paper carriage over to the beginning of the line. 
If an NFO or SFV file is opened & saved or transferred via FTP /TEXT (instead of FTP /BINARY) on a different platform than it was created on, then the line termination character is changed even though the file may look identical. You can use command line utility called AWK to switch from Windows to *nix linefeeds and back, to figure out which one was used on the original uploaded torrent. AWK comes with Git for Windows, which you can find here .
To convert a Windows file to *nix, enter:
 awk '{ sub("\r$", ""); print }' winfile.txt > unixfile.txt 
To convert a *nix file to Windows, enter:
 awk 'sub("$", "\r")' unixfile.txt > winfile.txt 
Another low-tech solution that works is to open a *nix file in Wordpad on windows and click Save, it will save with the CR added.
This solves the issue and allows the torrent to check to 100% about 90% of the time. If your NFO still doesn't check out then there might be something else wrong with it.

 Outside Seeding With ruTorrent 
Welcome to our outside seeding guide for ruTorrent/rTorrent, the most common client used by most of today's seedbox providers. Most of you will have purchased a new seedbox to help you build ratio and then come to find out you can't max out your blazing new upload pipe.  Part I: Finding Something Good To Outside Seed 
Note: Part I of this guide assumes you don't have access to other private trackers, if you do I highly recommend you get your releases from there as it will be very easy to find the exact same release in the same rar'ed state. 
Finding a release on a public tracker isn't always easy, you have to deal with people removing files, unraring the release, and modifying it various other ways; but if your only choice is public trackers they can still be an excellent source for outside seeding material if you take care to ensure everything is correct.
To start you will want to look at popular new releases on TL. (You can also start by looking for popular releases on the outside tracker first but that is purely user preference)
I usually recommend starting about 1/3 of the way down the page, you want releases that are a few hours old to give them time to find their way to public trackers; this makes it easier to find what you are looking for.
I found Safe House 720p BluRay X264-BLOW about 1/2 way down the front page of releases on TL. I usually recommend HD movies, Xbox 360 and PC games. TV episodes due to their small size and short time of relevance are not recommended.
Now that I have my release to outside seed I need to find it on a public tracker. After a couple minutes of searching I found it on a very popular public tracker but there is a problem. Even though the release names and size were near exactly the same and it appears to be the same movie, the uploader to the public tracker unrared the release and removed the sample and nfo. This is is a waste of time, and a common issue most new outside seeders have, the release can not be unrared (unless it is at TL) and you don't want to waste time trying to re-rar it as you usually will fail. 
I was unable to find the same Safe House release after some more searching so I decided to move on. Why am I including this fail in the guide? To let you know it can and will happen and to show you that you can't be discouraged and must move on. So let's keep on truckin.
Slightly further down the main TL page I found Mirror Mirror 2012 R5 LiNE XviD AC3-Voltage
The release isn't very popular yet, but I think it could be tomorrow morning and with the wait time crowd so I decide to go try and find it. Also the release isn't rar'ed on TL so that will make it easier to find it on publics.
I instantly find it on a public tracker
and it appears to have the needed nfo and sample files. It has some extra crap files that the public uploader added but that is fine, it will just be ignored in our process.
 Part II: Download The Release To ruTorrent 
So I download the release I found on the public tracker to ruTorrent just as normal. This guide assumes you know how to add a torrent to ruTorrent, if not please consider reading a basic ruTorrent guide first. A tip though, if your public tracker is using magnet links you need to paste those in to the “Torrent URL ” box in the add a torrent dialog and click “Add URL ”. It will look broken at first (show weird name and files, meta data), but let it go, it will change to the proper name and files after a minute or two.
Here you can see the file is downloading (slowly of course, its a public tracker after all) and you can also see the add torrent dialog box below which shows the Torrent URL as seen below 
 Part IIIa: Getting The Release Outside Seeding in ruTorrent 
Once the release has completed the download you want to grab the .torrent file from Torrent Leech and save it to your hard drive.
Now again click the “Add Torrent” button in ruTorrent. This time we must set a few things that are specific to outside seeding. 
First you want to tick “Don't add torrents name to path” and tick “Don't start the download automatically” so that they are both showing as CHECKED. 
Next click the 3 dots next to the “Directory” edit box to browse which will bring up a drop down list of all the torrents on your box. You want to choose the release you downloaded from the public tracker from the list. In my case there was some extra crap added to the directory name, that is OK, the directory names do not need to match.
Now click Browse for “Torrent File” and locate and select the .torrent file you downloaded from TL. 
Everything should be set like so: 
If all looks correct, click the “Add File” button. 
Now you should have the public torrent seeding in your client and the TL torrent but stopped. 
 Part IIIb: Force check to 100% 
Your next step is simple but key, you want to right click on the TL torrent that is stopped and choose “Force Re-Check”. This will go through a checking process that depending on the size of the torrent and server load can take several minutes to complete. It will say “Checking” as the status and will go to 100%. When it is complete it will show the amount of the torrent you have. Hopefully it is 100% (or very close)
If all went well you should have 2 torrents, the TL one should read 100% and paused like so: 
Right click on the TL torrent and click “Start”. If you had 100% the torrent will start seeding and congratulations you are outside seeding! (Probably should stop the public torrent at this point as they will mess up your upload stats, but do not choose remove and delete as this will delete the data you need!)
 Part IV: Things went wrong 
The dreaded 99%. This means your missing part of the release that was most likely stripped out of the public release, commonly an nfo or sample. Usually your best bet if after searching around the net and can't find it is to hop on our irc and ask politely for some assistance in the main channel. Many times a staff or helpful member will be able to grab what you need, they know you are trying hard. 
Now don't make this big mistake that is quite common. Public trackers usually have slow downloads so you may have the urge to add the .torrent from TL to your client and start seeding the 50% you have. DON'T! This is a common gotcha with outside seeding. The TL tracker will detect this as you downloading from TL and if this happens there is no way to fix it. Just make sure you have 100% before you recheck and start the torrent on TL. If the recheck says 90% just recheck it again until it says 100%.
 Part IV: Results 
My results were mediocre, I uploaded 6GB in about a day. The key though is that at 6GB uploaded your wait times are almost completely gone and I downloaded 0 from TL, all net gain! If you replicated these results you would only need to upload 1GB more to be done with any limitations. Also keep in mind this was not a very popular movie and R5's can be hit or miss popularity wise in general, but on a more popular 4GB torrent you could easily net over 100GB on a single torrent from a descent seedbox.

 Outside Seeding for uTorrent 
 Outside seeding is when instead of downloading the files from Torrentleech you instead download the files from another source and then use them to seed the Torrent on Torrentleech instead.
New users get the most out of outside seeding as it gives a boost to a users upload without having to download any files thus increasing thier ratio quickly. 
However, if your files you are using to “outside seed” do not match 100% then they will NOT work. This is because the hashcheck must be the same on your files obtained elsewhere and the files listed on the site.
For this example I will be using [HorribleSubs] Naruto Shippuuden ‐ 189 [720p].mkv however this will work with any other release as long as the files are exactly the same.
 Step 1 
First find a torrent on a public tracker that you think you might be able to find on Torrentleech. While looking I found the torrent [HorribleSubs] Naruto Shippuuden ‐ 189 [720p].mkv 
 Step 2 
Try to locate that torrent in Torrentleech this may not always be possible but in this case I found the exact same torrent here. Now that you have found it on Torrentleech download it from the public torrent site you found it in the Step 1.
 Step 3 
Wait till the torrent has finished when it has finished stop the torrent and download the .torrent file from Torrentleech you found in step 2 and open it with utorrent. 
 Step 4 
When opening the torrent in uTorrent you will see this window. Make sure to change the file path to match the torrent downloaded from the public tracker. 
 Do NOT change the tracker information located inside the .torrent file! 
In this case all the files match but if you have lots of files in the torrent and some don’t match make sure to untick those files and also untick Start torrent.
 Step 5 
uTorrent will now check the files you will get a window that looks something like this as it does. This can take quite a while depending on the size of the torrent.
 Step 6 
Check the file list of the torrent and make sure all the files are blue as anything that is red will be download. If a file is red right click it and choose don’t download this will stop it from downloading it.
 Step 7 
Start the torrent it will now seed it without having to download anything from Torrentleech. 
 What if the NFO doesn't match? 
Sometimes other places will slightly alter their torrent data including the NFO file and it may be necessary to change it back so that it matches the one on Torrentleech . If you don't do this then your torrent will NOT hashcheck to 100% which is essential in order to start seeding for you. 
If you don't have any wait times then vuze will overwrite the .NFO data to match the one on the site without you having to do anything. However, if you DO have wait times, you will need to complete the following steps to begin seeding.
If the torrent does not start seeding because it is stuck on 99.9% (Or similar) then there is usually an issue with the included .NFO file you are trying to match. If you look into the details of the torrent you will find the .NFO file and in most cases where it doesn't hashcheck to 100%, this is usually the cause. 
 Step 1 
Open the .nfo file in the torrent folder that wont hashcheck to 100% using notepad. Now click on the NFO tab on the torrent page on the site. You will see the following.
 Step 2 
Once you click the button that says then the NFO will show the text data of the NFO instead of an image.
For example, Here is how a random torrent NFO looks as a generated image before you press the button:
Now press the “Switch to Text” button, the image will change to this:
 Step 3 
When you have changed the NFO into text, start from the top left and copy the entire NFO down to the bottom. Doing so ensures that the data will match when you save your newly ammended NFO file.
Using the example NFO shown previously, it should highlight and show as follows:
As you can see we have highlighted “blank data” as well as the text data. This is essential to ensure it will be exactly the same as yours when you save it.
 Step 4 
Now all you have to do is overwrite all data in your opened NFO with the data you have copied from the NFO onsite and save it. Do NOT rename it or save as any other format other than .NFO otherwise it wont work.
 Step 5 
Open uTorrent and select the torrent that you have just fixed. Press stop, right click and choose . The program will now hashcheck the torrent data and “should” now display as having 100% of the data which allows it to seed for you.
