 Part Seeding for uTorrent 
 Summary: Part Seeding is when you only select some of the .rar files inside the torrent to download and only
seed those. This works best with large releases such as games (Xbox 360, PC, PS3, Wii - In that order resspectively.
 Packs should be avoided like the plague for new users until you get your wait times down or completely lifted. Once you do, try newly released TV shows that are popular at the time. It is best to jump on them as soon as you possible so that you can maximise your chances of getting a good upload off them.
Please avoid anything old as anyone who would want them will have gotten them by that stage. If old torrents show a lot of leechers, those are in fact part seeders so avoid those at all costs. We have lost many members who have made that mistake with packs.
 Part seeding is great to get up your ratio as you would only have to downloaded a small amount of the torrent data and many people will want to get those files from you, epecially if you jump on the torrent as early as you can. If you part seed on a cam for example, I suggest only downloading the sample as users tend to check the quality before downloading the whole thing. (Just through personal experience)
 Part seeding has the draw back for new users that have wait times. In order to get around this see outside seeding. 
For this guide I will be using the Xbox 360 release Naruto Ultimate Ninja Storm 2 PAL XBOX360‐STRANGE 
 Step 1 
Find a newly released torrent. In this case it’s Naruto Ultimate Ninja Storm 2 PAL XBOX360‐STRANGE and download the .torrent file for it. If possible, dont allow your client to automatically start downloading the release.
 Step 2 
Open the file in uTorrent. When opened you will be presented with this.
Now at the moment if you select ok, it will start to download all the .rars and this is not what we want.
 Step 3 
Hit “select none” and your window should now look like this.
Now, while on the same window, please untick the box that says Start Torrent so we dont start downloading yet. You should see it at the top and it will look like this once unticked.
At this stage uTorrent will not download anything from the torrent, which is not what we want but it IS necessary for us to achieve our aim of this guide.
 Step 4 
Now, the REALLY important part. 
Just randomly select about 2‐3 files, If its a movie, grab the sample along with some of the first and last parts of the release. For example if a release has 63 rars at 97.5Mb each, grab the sample, then the first two rars and last two rars. This is because some clients prioritise the first and last rars in a torrent to ensure they can complete. (Dont bother with samples on dvdrips as people rarely grab those.
You can choose to download more rars if you want but I recommend about 2‐3 for beginning and unril you get used to how the method works for part seeding. NOTE If you choose to do more make sure you have a good upload speed (5MBits+) otherwise it will be really hard to seed (Upload) back what you have leeched (downloaded).
 Step 5 
Click “OK” . Now it will only download the rars you selected. Sometimes it may grab a small portion of other rars you didnt want but thats nothing to worry about and those will part seed for you also anyway. This is especially true of seedboxes.
You have now finished this guide :D. For added benefit leave it seeding as long as possible because the longer you leave it to seed the more you upload. Even when it appears as if nobody wants it anymore, its always beneficial to leave it there as people dont always download their torrents at once. Some users grab their releases in stages due to restrictions on their isp for example, like being able to download unlimited after midnight. (Virgin Media do this but thats purely an example to explain the reasoning behind leaving it as long as space allows)
Guide made by Ronan from Torrentleech

 I have a seedbox, What do I do? 
You need to inform staff that you are using a seedbox by adding your seedbox in your profile. You can do this yourself, just click on your name in the upper right corner, then click on profile. There you can select the tab 'seedbox' and add the information. You will need to provide the IP of the box, the provider and the speed its being sold at (e.g. 100mbit or 1gbit). Other information is optional.
 Why do I need to do this? 
The answer is quite simple. If you do not report the usage of a seedbox then there is a high chance that you may find your account disabled for suspected cheating. This is largely due to excessive speeds that your ISP simply cannot handle.
 Are my details safe? 
Yes. Account security is extremely important to us and only staff are able to see your seedbox IP. This is NEVER shared with anyone else.
 Why did I receive a speedtest request when I have a seedbox? 
This can happen when you haven't reported your seedbox to site staff. The best thing to do is provide the speedtest add your seedbox details via your profile. Do this as soon as you can, as failure to respond can result in your account being disabled.

Today we have updated Torrentleech with a lot of bugfixes and two new functions: a proper request system and achievements! In this post we will tell you how these work.
Please keep in mind we are currently releasing these systems as BETA. We are looking forward for your feedback to improve them as we go, so make sure to jump on our forum and let us know what you think!
 How will the system work? 
If are looking for a release that isn't on the site yet, you can now request it via our new request system. All you need is the proper amount of points to make the request (this is based on your user class) and some basic information as to what you are requesting. Once the request has been made, any other member with Power User class or above can fill your request. The torrent used to fill the request will not be visible until the request is approved or declined . Points will only be transferred after approval and will be deducted from the requestees account and added to the account of the member who uploaded the torrent.
 Update: 
A lot of users tend to 'forget' to approve their requests. For operational purposes we have since removed the manual approval for TV shows and Movie requests. They will be filled on upload. Be aware that requests which are not properly filled will still get reported and we will take appropriate action if users continue to have their uploaded torrents rejected as a fill.
 Who can make a request? 
Any member can make a request, as long as they have the required points for it.
 Will my requests be limited like they were in the forums? 
No, you can make as many requests as you have points.
 What will a request cost? 
 User Class Cost 
 Registered 1000 points per request 
 Power User 800 points per request 
 Super User 700 points per request 
 Extreme User 600 points per request 
 TL GOD 400 points per request 
 VIP FREE requests! 
 Who can fill a request? 
Any member that has Power User class or above. Unlike before you do not need to be an Uploader on Torrentleech to be able to fill requests.
 So how do I fill a request? 
You can browse requests and see if there are any that you are able to fill, either with a torrent already on TL or by uploading a whole new torrent. You can use our upload form directly from the request page, if you want to actually upload a new torrent you can use our Wiki article about it for more guidance.
 What happens after a torrent has been uploaded and is pending review? 
The requester will get a notification and can now review the pending torrent. The request will be locked for other users who want to fill it. If the requester approves it, the torrent will be made visible and the points will be transferred from the requester to the uploader of the torrent. The request will then be marked as filled. If the requester disapproves the pending torrent, it will be deleted and the request will be unlocked and marked as open once again.
 How will you ensure quality if any member can now upload a torrent to fill a request? 
The torrent will not be visible until it has been approved by either the requester of a member of staff. Once approved the uploaded torrent will be visible on the main page. All torrents uploaded by a member other than Uploaders will be listed for review by our staff in any case, so we can ensure quality and safety of all torrents.
Requests for applications however, will only be visible once they have been reviewed by staff as these present a greater risk for malware than other torrents.
 What happens if I request a reseed of an existing torrent? 
Your request will be most likely be accepted as filled, as the torrent is already on the site. You will lose your points. Don't request reseeds as a new request, instead use the reseed button on the dead torrent.
 How will you deal with abuse? 
We will be actively monitoring requests and there are some back-end functions to aid us with that. Any members who are found abusing the system in any way will have their rights to make and/or fill requests revoked. In extreme cases we will deal with the situation accordingly.

 RSS for uTorrent 
 RSS feeds are great for downloading your favourite TV Shows every week and will do so automaticly without you having to do anything. 
Be warned though, if you don’t set up your filters correctly it could end up downloading a lot of torrents and ruining your ratio. 
 Be sure to keep your RSS refresh interval above 5 minutes, or your IP will be temporarily banned. 
 Step 1: Get your RSS Key 
 Skip to step 2 if you already have an RSS key, otherwise go to your profile and hit [edit profile]. 
 Scroll down to the [ RSS options] and click the button to enable your RSS access (off by default) and click Save. 
 Scroll back to the [ RSS options] and you will see two different RSS links:
 Latest top 100 torrents RSS Link: feed for the last 100 torrents uploaded to the site.
 Latest 24 hours torrents RSS Link: all torrent uploaded in the past 24 hours.
 These keys are obviously no longer valid 
Choose the link your prefer and go to step 2. 
 Step 2: Add the feed to your client 
 Open uTorrent. Click add RSS feed.
 Enter the link you got from step 1.
 Then click OK.
 Step 3: Set up your filter 
 Go to Options → RSS Downloader
 You will now see this window
 In this case I will be using Naruto however you will need to change what you enter to get different results. First we need to Press the Add button. After we do that we will see this.
 You will want to rename this to what u want the filter to be about in this case I’m going to call it Naruto. Now we need to fill in the fields so it gets the things we want.
 Filter: Add the keywords here you want it to look for.
The filter is the most important field and doesn’t work how most think it does. It will try to match your filter from left to right character for character.
So your entire phrase has to be in there somewhere in that order.
This is where the ‘*’ and ‘?’ characters come in. ‘*’ is a wild card and means any character and multiples of them. ‘?’ on the other hand is any single character not multiple.
For example if the name of the torrent is [HorribleSubs] Naruto Shippuuden - ### [720p] then we need to match that.
So for this we could do *Naruto* - However this will download anything with Naruto in it including games and different qualities such as 720p, 1080p, different seasons etc.
We could do Naruto*720p – This will only download the 720p one. However if there are multiple groups releasing this it will get them all. To avoid this we could set the filter as *HorribleSubs*Naruto*720p* . This will only get the releases we want instead of downloading multiple variations.
It's best not to make the filter too specific as a single typo or change in name formatting could break it such as a group using ”.” or “_”instead of a space.
 Not - Add the keywords here that if it contains any that you don’t want to download

 Feed - The feed it will look at to find the torrent
 Quality - The quality you want it in, this can cause things to break for certain releases.
 Episode Number - The episodes u want so for example 1×12-14 will look for season 1 and will only download Episodes 12-14.
 Smart ep. Filter - This will try to only download the right episodes. So if you last downloaded episode 5 it won’t download 1-5 and will only download episode 6 next.
 Be warned this button doesn’t always work so if the feeds aren’t working try un-ticking it.
 Minimal Interval - The minimal amount of time till it will look to download another episode. If you are having problems with the feeds change this to always match
 Note: All changes are saved as they are made so don’t freak out that there is no save or OK button.
 Step 4: Rinse and repeat

 rTorrent on Windows (using Cygwin) 
 Introduction 
rTorrent is a widely popular torrent client for Linux. Have you ever wished that you can run it directly on Windows? Well, using a program known as Cygwin, you can! Unfortunately, the program that usually accompanies rTorrent, known as ruTorrent, will not work due to XMLRPC not being supported on Cygwin. This isn't too much of an issue though, since you can navigate and use rtorrent using its own interface - it just doesn't look as cool. Similarly, we won't be supporting autodl-irssi, but since you are using Windows you could use TLTD instead.
 Installation 
 You may be tempted to start straight away, but we advise to read the remainder of this guide, especially the Advanced Tips below before you start installing. 
 Obtain the latest installer from Cygwin 
 Install using the default settings or customize to your needs.
 When prompted for “A Download Site” just pick one in your country. This is to install Cygwin itself, and not related torrents yet.
 On the next step, we can add Packages to install. Use the screenshot below to see what you should do.
 You should see that rtorrent is part of the packages on the Review and confirm changes screen.
 The setup will now install Cygwin, rtorrent and its dependent files.
 Click Finish to end the installation. If you would prefer no shortcuts, uncheck the boxes first.
 Configuration 
You will now have an application called “Cygwin64 Terminal” which you can launch. Do so now. You should end up with a screen like this:
We'll set up your rtorrent preferences file straight away by copying the sample file to your home folder. To do so, run the following command inside the Cygwin terminal:
 cp /usr/share/doc/rtorrent/rtorrent.rc ~/.rtorrent.rc 
If you are simply returned to your prompt, then this means the command was successful.
Using your favorite text editor (we highly recommend Notepad++, since it understands Linux line feeds), edit the file and make your preferred settings. Assuming you used the default installation folder, you will find the .rtorrent.rc file in %systemdrive%\cygwin64\home\%username%
The following settings should be set. Remember to remove the # at the start of the line so that you uncomment them:
 directory.default.set = ./torrents # This will put your downloaded torrents into its own folder, rather than just placing them all in your cygwin home folder
 schedule2 = watch_directory,5,5,load.start=./watch/*.torrent # This will set your watch folder, and automatically load new torrents placed here
 network.port_range.set = 61000-61010 # A range of 10 ports is recommended. Remember to forward these in from your firewall so that you are connectable
 dht.mode.set = disable # Required setting for our tracker
If you are needing to do some extended debugging (for example, tracker debug logging), add the following lines to the end and comment/uncomment where needed (lines that start with a # are commented out and not processed):
 log.open_file = "rtorrent", ./log/rtorrent.log
log.open_file = "tracker", ./log/tracker.log
log.open_file = "storage", ./log/storage.log
log.add_output = "info", "rtorrent"
#log.add_output = "critical", "rtorrent"
#log.add_output = "error", "rtorrent"
#log.add_output = "warn", "rtorrent"
#log.add_output = "notice", "rtorrent"
#log.add_output = "debug", "rtorrent"
#log.add_output = "dht_debug", "tracker"
log.add_output = "tracker_debug", "tracker"
#log.add_output = "storage_debug", "storage" 
 Usage 
Before starting it for the first time, you have to create some folders. Run the following commands from your Cygwin terminal window.
 mkdir ~/log
mkdir ~/session
mkdir ~/torrents
mkdir ~/watch 
Once you have saved your configuration file, you can start rtorrent. Start it simply by typing rtorrent 
You should see a screen like this, which shows that it is working.
To be sure that things are looking good, find and download a freeleech torrent, and save it to your watch folder.
Navigating the application is just a matter of learning some hotkeys. The most common ones are as follows:
To view a complete list of rtorrent hotkeys, visit the user guide 
To close Cygwin gracefully, shut down rtorrent first (Ctrl+q), so that it sends the final announce to the tracker, and then type “exit” to quit Cygwin.
 Advanced Tips 
 Install to Alternate location 
Cygwin runs as your locally logged on user. If you need to install it to a network share or an alternate drive, you are welcome to do so during the installation, but you MUST map a network drive first. You cannot use UNC.
It is important that your drive be mapped every time you wish to use Cygwin64, or you will simply be unable to start it.
 Download to NAS 
An alternative to mapping a network drive and installing Cygwin64 on your mapped drive, you can create a symbolic link from your local drive to your network drive instead, so that all your downloads go there. Assuming you used the guide above to download everything to your “torrents” folder under %systemdrive%\cygwin64\home\%username%, and you would like this folder to now be on a network share, we can use “mklink”, a windows command-line tool to create symbolic links. Follow these steps:
 close rtorrent (control-Q)
 open a command prompt (start → cmd.exe)
 in the command prompt, type cd %systemdrive%\cygwin64\home\%username% to go to the folder where the “torrents” folder exists
 Rename the torrents folder to something else, for example, rename torrents torrents.old 
 Create the symbolic link to your network path - for example, mklink /D torrents \\moon\data\Download 
 Move your downloaded torrents from torrents.old to torrents so that rtorrent can resume them when you restart it.
 start rtorrent
NOTE: If you get access denied like in my screenshot below when renaming the folder, it's simply because you have a lock on a file or folder (like File explorer window open, or media file open). Close it and try again.

 What else should you know about seedboxes 
 So which seedbox should you get 
 What is a seedbox? 
You might have heard or seen seedboxes being mentioned somewhere. The word seedbox implies exactly what it is: a box to seed your torrents with. It is a server, usually connected to a high speed network with improved peering (connectability) to other torrent users.
Check this youtube video : –> What is a Seedbox? - Introduction to Seedbox ←-
 Can you recommend a Seedbox provider ? 
We highly recommend Seedit4.me !
 Can I use any provider ? 
You can use any provider you want, just keep in mind there are huge differences and not all providers will give you the same results.
 Do I need to let TL know if I get one? 
Yes, you can read more about it here .
 Why do I need one 
You do not need one, but it makes your life on private trackers easier. If you have a slow connection though, it's almost a must to get a seedbox.
 Speed: You let your seedbox do the downloading and uploading of torrents you want, and I can assure you it will be much faster than you would do it at home (downloading and uploading a like). This will give you an extra upload buffer and will enable you to acquire more content. 
 Free my network: You are a part of a private torrent site which requires you to seed as much as you can and build a ratio. That usually means leaving your torrent client open taking most of your home traffic (your upload speed) away for seeding purposes. A seedbox will seed for you, as much as you want without affecting your home network for one bit. 
 ISP issues: While there are some who have not witnessed traffic shaping /throttling, a lot us are well familiar with it: your ISP (internet service provider) is messing with your Bandwidth. You might be downloading way slower than you can or will barely be able to upload at all. A seedbox will free you from worrying about it at all.
 Anonymity 
A seedbox is pretty anonymous. If you ever got a DMCA notice from your ISP , and you are afraid that the wonderful MPAA/RIAA are looking at you as we speak, fear no more. Bittorent is a file sharing protocol where you share bits and pieces with other people in the swarm. This means everyone in your swarm can look at your IP, sometimes those likeable creatures such as the MPAA/RIAA are able to do so. The seedbox will give you an extra layer of anonymity, since the only IP that those people in the swarm will see is for that seedbox. You can even use a VPN as well to act as an extra level of security but that is covered in another guide. 
 No matter where you are 
 If you have a seedbox, you can remote desktop to your server, download the .torrent file and add it to your seedbox client no matter where you are. Thus enabling you to add torrents at other locations than your home link. And it doesn’t end there:
 You can ftp to your seedbox from wherever you are, and share those files you downloaded with friends, family , gf’s/bf’s or even your favorite massage parlor. There’s nothing like torrenting with a massage with a happy ending, trust me.
 Different type of seedboxes 
 Shared/slot 
 The most popular and affordable solution for your seedbox needs. A shared seedbox is a big dedicated server which shares its resources among the users of that server. 
 You as a user get a part of the HDD while you share the ram, cpu and of course the line speed with a bunch of others. The main difference from a semi-dedi server is that the amount of people you share this resources with is much larger. This depends from one provider to another, while most of those providers are actually resellers who bought a dedi server and resell it as a shared seedbox. With some providers you can chose the torrent client you can install, and with some it comes pre installed. 
 While it is the most affordable solution for a seedbox, the sharing of resources can lead to issues with stability, speed or downtime.
 Dedicated server 
The ultimate seedbox experience. A dedicated server (dedi) is basically a server which sits in a huge datacenter connected to super turbo fast internet lines. If you rent a dedi, you rent it all by yourself without sharing the resources of the server with anyone else. This means, your dedi server line speed, ram, cpu, HDD write/array is all for you (and your friends if you’re looking for a cheaper solution). It's also the most expensive option.
 Semi dedicated 
The concept is basically like the dedi servers, but the only difference is that you share the resources of the server with a few more users (which you know nothing about). That doesn’t mean they have access to your files, but you usually share the ram,cpu,hdd and of course, the Bandwidth with a few others. It is a more affordable solution to people who can’t afford buying a dedicated server. The plans most providers offer for semi-dedi’s vary from one to another, and with them the amount of people you share the server and line speed as well. Usually the resources are shared between up to 4-5 people, but then again they could be shared between only two, depends on the host and the plan they offer. Most of the semi-dedi’s comes pre managed, while you have the choice of choosing which torrent client you want, as well of other applications you might want to install. The semi dedi is the closest thing to a dedi server- offers more resources than a shared server, but is more affordable to people who can’t buy a dedi. 
 What else should you know about seedboxes 
 Seedboxes can be highly addictive. There are some people that believe the faster speeds they will get will contribute to building a bigger ePen0r. Let alone the comfort of being able to download the content and share it with your friends and family. The simple truth is, your helping out the community by allowing them to download from you at a good speed which is why you yourself are able to download at a good speed in the first place. Just think about that for a moment.
 It’s not all roses and violets:
 A lot of the shared seedboxes providers/resellers are overcrowding their servers to the point that the speeds are worse than your home link. Always Google a bit and ask your tracker friends for their opinion on one distributor or another. 
 Beware of free seedboxes- not just because of the quality, but because you don’t know who is behind them. Usually these seedboxes are disallowed on TL, especially Debrid variations.
 Always look at the technical specifications of the seedbox/s: some providers mention how many users will share the same server, and others don’t. Always ask about this. Keep in mind that too many users all downloading/uploading at the same time on the same server might kill the performance. All tech factors play a role, not just the line speed: RAM, CPU and most important are how many people are sharing the same HDD.
 Always check if the bandwidth per month is unlimited/unmetered, and if it isn’t, know your limits. A lot of them get capped after you upload a certain amount of data outside the datacenter of that supplier and your stuck with it until the next time you renew in which case its useless. 
 Don't forget to add the seedbox to your profile here .
 So which seedbox should you get 
Don’t go over your budget. Decide what kind of server do you want: Dedi, semi or shared and see if there are any plans that will work out for you. Always look at the small prints and the provider faq and always google for opinions about this supplier or another. If you decide to get a seedbox but still aren't sure where to get one, call into our irc channel and ask the regulars there for there thoughts. Some will be only too happy to help, staff will assist you where possible as well.

 TorrentLeech.org Wiki

 Table of Contents
 What are slots and why does TorrentLeech use them? 
 So how many slots do I have? 
 Why do I get a "Access denied - Torrents Limit exceeded " error? 
 Why do i get a "Connection limit exceeded! You may only leech from one location at a time" error? 
 What are slots and why does TorrentLeech use them? 
Download slots dictate how many torrents you can download at once. We use this system to encourage our users to keep a good ratio on the tracker. Be aware that part seeding a torrent also counts as using a download slot.
 So how many slots do I have? 
In all cases the seeding slots are unlimited. At any time, you can check your available slots in the member bar on the top of the page underneath the logo. You should also know that the slots for every user are calculated every 30min. Which means that if you cross a ratio barrier for more or less slots the tracker will need up to 30 min to be informed of this change, in spite of the maximum slots that you can see on your member bar. You can however update the tracker manually with some clients but bear in mind that doing this too often will result in tracker issues.
 Your ratio Available download slots 
 0.50 or lower 1 slot 
 0.60 or lower 2 slots 
 0.70 or lower 3 slots 
 0.85 or lower 4 slots 
 0.86 and above unlimited slots 
 Why do I get a "Access denied - Torrents Limit exceeded " error? 
You will see this message once you are trying to download more torrents simultaneously than your download slots allow. To fix it you simply need to have patience, as one slot frees up another download will start. If you are stuck on this error for some reason, you can also stop all your torrents for 30 minutes, then start the torrent you wish to download manually.
Be aware that partially downloaded torrents still use up one of your slots, even if you are seeding it because you only needed one file!
 Why do i get a "Connection limit exceeded! You may only leech from one location at a time" error? 
This is an error associated with the passkey system. You may leech each torrent from one location only. If you dont leech the torrent from a second location, and you still get this problem, reset your passkey in your control panel and redownload the torrent (also redownload any other torrent you leech at the same time, or you will get an invalid passkey error)
The maximum permitted simultaneous connections per torrent are 3. 1 leech + 2 seeds or 3 seeds from any single location.

 What are TL Points? 
 What are the bonus rates?

 Amount of seeders 
 User Class 
 How points are calculated? 
 What can I use the points for? 
 What are TL Points? 
TL points are awarded for seeding completed torrents over time and will be used to buy goodies from the marketplace. The marketplace is constantly evolving, so be sure to check it regularly. 
So how do these points work exactly? To be awarded the points that go with this new system, you will need the following ingredients:
 You must have downloaded the torrent fully (100%) from TL.
 Cross-seeded torrents will not earn TL Points.
 The torrent has to be active.
 You must seed a complete torrent, part seeding will not yield any points.
 The torrent has to be at least 10MB in size.
 It will grant you the appropriate amount of points per 1 hour of seeding (see below).
 The point(s) will be added after you have accumulated 1 hour of seeding, however that may happen.
 You will receive your points even if there are 0 leechers.
 You can only receive points for 200 torrents at the same time.
 These 200 torrents are made up out of two groups: 100 torrents based on size and 100 torrents based on amount of seeders.
 The size-group torrents will be sorted from large to small, meaning your largest torrents will be the ones accumulating points.
 The seeder-group torrents will be sorted by amount of seeders from lowest to highest (highest being 5).
 The site will update at least once an hour, but not in real time.
The current base amount for a torrent is: 0.04 points per hour.
 What are the bonus rates? 
There are different bonus rates based on size, your user class and whether the torrent has more than 5 seeders or not.
 Torrent size 
These bonus points are calculated based on the base points you receive for the torrent.
 Minimum torrent size Maximum torrent size Bonus amount 
 over 1GB 2GB 2% 
 over 2GB 5GB 4% 
 over 5GB 10GB 8% 
 over 10GB 10% 
 Amount of seeders 
These bonus points are calculated based on the base points you receive for the torrent, the bonus is always 5% per torrent.
 User Class 
These bonus points are calculated based on the total sum of the TL points accruing, including the two bonus point amounts mentioned above.
 User class Bonus amount 
 Normal User 0% 
 Power User 3% 
 Super User 5% 
 Extreme User 6% 
 TL God 8% 
 VIP User 10% 
 How points are calculated? 
Points are calculated using the following formula: 
 (base points + (base points * size bonus) + (base points * rare bonus)) * (100% + class bonus) 
Example for a 15GB torrent with 3 seeders for a Super user: 
 (0.04 + (0.04 * 10%) + (0.04 * 5%)) * 105% 
The result is 0.0483 bonus points per hour.
 What can I use the points for? 
There is a new tab on your profile page, where you can spend the points you have accumulated. As the points have just recently been introduced, not many options are available and more will follow over time. Current you have the following options:
 Reward Cost 
 1 GB Upload 90 points 
 2.5 GB Upload 180 points 
 5 GB Upload 300 points 
 10 GB Upload 540 points 
 100 GB Upload 5.000 points 
 250 GB Upload 12.000 points

 User Ratios 
 How does my ratio evolve? 
 What's MY ratio? 
 What is the minimum ratio I should keep? 
 User Ratios 
The ratio you keep on TorrentLeech is very important. The ratio is your uploaded amount of data, devided by your downloaded amount of data. Some examples:
 Your current upload Your current download Your ratio 
 10GB 10GB 1.0 
 20GB 10GB 2.0 
 200GB 300GB 0.667 
 How does my ratio evolve? 
Let's say you current ratio is 1.0. In order to keep that ratio from falling, you will need to upload each torrent to exactly 1.0 as well. As soon as you upload more or less, your overall ratio will also rise or drop. 
 An example: 
Your current ratio upload is 100GB and your current download is also 100GB, you have a great ratio of 1:
 Uploaded Downloaded Ratio 
 100GB 100GB 1.0 
If you download a 10GB torrent now without uploading anything else, your ratio will fall because of your new traffic amounts:
 Uploaded Downloaded Ratio 
 100GB 110GB 0.909 
Your ratio will rise again once you start uploading data. If your torrent reaches 10GB up, you total amount of data will be 110/110= 1.0 once again:
 Uploaded Downloaded Ratio 
 110GB 110GB 1.0 
 What's MY ratio? 
 On any page just look at the banner on top of your screen, it will show you a few things, just hoover over the different numbers to see what they correspond with.
 It's important to distinguish between your overall ratio and the individual ratio on each torrent you may be seeding or leeching. The overall ratio takes into account the total uploaded and downloaded from your account since you joined the site. The individual ratio takes into account those values for each torrent.
 What is the minimum ratio I should keep? 
 Every user is expected to maintain an overall site ratio of 0.4 after downloading 6GB. If you fail to do this the site will automatically warn your account and you will have 7 days to get back to an overal account ratio of 0.4 The warning will automatically be removed as long as your account is still over the 0.4 minimum site ratio as soon as it expires. It will NOT remove itself as soon as you reach a ratio of 0.4 
 There is also a per torrent minimum which is also 1:1 If you are not able to seed the torrent to 1:1 then you will need to leave it seeding for the required amount of time for your user class , or you could receive a warning for Hit & Run.

 Vuze - How To Disable DHT 
 DHT needs to be disabled to ensure Vuze sends the correct stat's to TL's tracker, failure to do this will result in warnings and your eventual ban.
Guide made using the Classic Gui, the steps to do this are outlined below.
 Tip - For those of you who do not like the Vuze interface you can choose to use the Classic interface of Azureus instead of the Vuze one, loosing all the fancy trimmings which you may feel are not needed for you.
 Go To > Tools > Options > Interface > Start > Under "Display Vuze UI Chooser" > Click "Show" and choose "Classic", now just restart "Vuze" 
 Fire up Vuze and change to it's advanced mode.
 Go To > Tools > Options > Mode check "Advanced" 
 On the “Connection” Tab under “Peer Sources” - “Select the default permitted sources for peer connections” only check “From a tracker”
 On the “Plugins” Tab select “Distributed DB” and uncheck “Enable the distributed database”
 On the “Plugins” Tab select “Distributed Tracker” and uncheck “Only track normal torrents when their tracker is unavailable”
 On the “Classic Sharing” Tab check “Private torrent - only accept peers from the tracker” (This should automatically grey out and disable “Allow decentralized tracking when tracker is unavailable”)
 Save and restart Vuze You will now see “DHT Disabled” on the bottom of the main Vuze window. If you don't, go through this Vuze guide again and restart the program.
 Bear in mind, Vuze used to be known as Azureus but they are the same program regardless.

 Trace: » why_your_uploads_are_stuck_at_zero 
 Table of Contents
 Why Are My Uploads So Slow? 
 Making Sure You're Connectable 
 Your Torrents Suck 
 You're Not Outside Seeding Enough 
 Your Connection is SLOW 
 Back to the FAQ 
 Why Are My Uploads So Slow? 
This is the most common question we get from new users, especially users new to private trackers in general. If your uploads are stuck at zero (or aren't seeding well at all) then listen up and take note! First lets make sure your setup correctly to seed.
Here's a special TIP just for you: Did you know that you won't be warned for low ratio until you have downloaded 6GB? If you haven't downloaded 6GB yet, DONT. But how will you seed if you cant download? We will get to that.
 Making Sure You're Connectable 
If your not connectable, you will have massive trouble seeding. In most cases you wont be able to seed at all. If your uploads are literally stuck at zero, make sure you check this first!
There is already a guide that covers this and it can be found here: How to Open your Ports . Basically you must make sure your incoming torrent port is forwarded at your router. There are many ways to do this including UPNP, etc. Google is your friend, there are guides for doing this for almost every router on the market. Now is also a good time to ensure your DHT/PEX/LPD is OFF. Set it OFF. A guide can be found here for Utorrent and for Vuze 
Is your torrent client showing green at the bottom? Is the torrent port you picked in utorrent showing as connectable HERE? Ok good, time to move on.
 Your Torrents Suck 
Yes, most likely the torrents you are trying to seed are old and well seeded. 
You may say “But pack xyz shows 5000 leechers and only 40 seeders! Why isnt it seeding?” No. No. No. It does not have 5000 leechers. These are part seeders, and why we are on the subject STAY AWAY FROM PACKS. Packs are the worst things to download when new no matter what for this reason. You can read more about part seeding here for uTorrent and for Vuze 
Another common mistake is downloading TV episodes and thinking you will make good ratio on this. Usually you will not. Some of my personal favorites when building ratio are popular new movie releases in 720p, popular xbox and pc games that are newly released, and if your outside seeding 1080 releases.
“So your saying I am screwed?” No, you are not. Because your savoir, Outside Seeding is our next subject. 
 You're Not Outside Seeding Enough 
The number 1 way for new users to make ratio here is to outside seed and the good news is that it's easier than you might think. For more details you can read this guide: Outside seeding with uTorrent and this one: Outside seeding with Vuze but in short you are downloading a torrent from elsewhere and then using that data to seed to TL without costing you any Download! 
This is vitaly important in creating a buffer that you can work with so as to get past any limitations and subsequently be able to download and seed new torrents.
Did you know that if you have 100% of the torrent, you can seed it to TL and bypass all limitations ?
My outside seeding tip of the day: If you are not on any other private trackers and must download from public ones, one easy way to make sure your getting the exact same release in RAR format is to grab a file name from the release and google for this filename. If you are having trouble finding anything at all to seed, give this a shot.
For every release you outside seed you are beating out all the other new users who didn't read this (or the many other helpful guides on our wiki) and when they jump on the torrent after the limitations have ended, you will already be there to seed it to them! Win!
 Your Connection is SLOW 
So you outside seeded with 10 brand new torrents and even though your connection is 50mbit you can only seed at 500Kb/s (for example). Well there could be several reasons. Number 1, “50mbit connection” means nothing. That is your download speed and since 99% of all broadband connections are asynchronous, your upload speed is way lower than your download. You need the 2nd number, for example: 50/5. This would indicate 50mbit download and 5mbit upload. 5mbit upload is likely to get you 500K/s. 
In the situation where you know your upload speed, lets say 50/20, and you can still only get 500Kb/s this is because your competing against many many seedboxes. Seedboxes start at 100/100 (100mbit upload) and unfortunately there is nothing you can do other than rent a seedbox or get a faster connection in this case. For example, I have 50/25 connection at my house but when I seed from home I am lucky to get 1 or 2MB/s upload rate to TL. If I seed these same torrents from my seedbox I am likely to get 5-10MB/s. The more bandwith you have to offer, the more likely other people's clients are going to pick you to download from. 
For this reason I personally recommend (and use) a seedbox. If you are interested in learning more, see here for information on seedboxes: Seedboxes - All you need to know 
If you've gotten this far you are most likely already on your way to fixing those pesky 0/kbs seeding torrents, my last tip is to keep them going too! Every single extra torrent you have seeding is another possible hit and after a while many of those seedbox users will have deleted your torrents from their client to make room for more, one of the best ways to gain an advantage on all those users with seedboxes when you dont have one is to have old torrents seeding for a long time.
Good luck!

由管理员仔细斟酌后分配给他们认为对于站点某方面有特殊贡献的用户。 （任何索取贵宾等级的要求将被自动无视） Retiree（隐世豪杰） 由管理员授予。 Uploader（CP0） 由管理员分配。 Moderator（本部中将） 无需多问，我们会找到你的！ 为什么我的朋友不能加入 用户数目有所限制（你可以查看“首页->站点数据->上限”）。当达到那个数目时，我们会停止接受新成员。 怎样自定义头像 首先，找一个你喜欢的图片，当然了它不能违反我们的规则。然后你要找一个存放它的图床，然后将其 URL 粘贴到你的控制面板的头像 URL 部分。 数据统计 最常见的数据未能得到更新的原因 服务器过载/未响应。只要尝试着保持会话直到服务器恢复响应 (不推荐连续手动刷新，这样会加重服务器负载)。 你正在使用不稳定的客户端。如果你想要使用测试版或者 CVS 版本，你需要自己承担由此带来的风险。 最佳的尝试 如果你当前正下载/上传的种子并不在你的用户详情页面中，你可以等一会或者强制进行手动更新。 确保你正确地关闭了客户端软件，否则 Tracker 服务器无法收到"event=completed"的信号。 如果 Tracker 服务器挂了，不要停止上传。只要在你退出客户端之前服务器恢复工作，所有的数据都会得到正确地更新。 为什么我正在下载做种的一个种子会在我的详情页面中被列出多次 如果因为某些原因(比方说死机，客户端失去响应)你的客户端非正常退出并且你又重新打开它，它会被分配到一个全新的 Peer ID, 这样它显示为一个全新的种子。而旧的种子将永远不会收到“event=completed”或“event=stopped”的信号，因此将一直被列出直到 Tracker 清理超时的 Peer。 无视了它就可以了，它最后会消失的。 为什么我已经完成取消的种子仍然在我的详情页面里 有一些客户端，比如说 TorrentStorm 和 Nova Torrent，在取消或者完成一个任务的时候不能向 Tracker 服务器正确发送信号。在那样的情况下，Tracker 服务器将一直保持等待信号的状态（因此会一直列出种子的状态为做种/下载的状态）直到 Tracker 清理超时的 Peer。无视了它就可以了，它最后会消失的。 多-ip我可以从不同的电脑登录下载吗 是的，目前 Tracker 服务器支持单个用户从任意个数的 IP 地址同时访问/下载。然而，对于单种是有限制的。对于每个种子，最多允许 3 个做种的连接，最多只允许 1 个下载的连接（这意味着，对于某个种子你一次只能在一个地方下载）。 发布 为什么我不能发布种子 请看上传者资格。 我需要满足哪些条件才能加入发布小组呢 你所必须满足的条件： 对于制作特效字幕/双语字幕/高质量字幕有热情 如果你认为你符合以上条件，那么不要犹豫，联系管理吧。 记住！ 仔细填写你的申请！确保申请中包含你的上传速度以及你计划发布的内容的类型。只有仔细填写并且经过慎重考虑的申请才会纳入我们的视野。 我可以发布你们这里的种子到别的-tracker-服务器么 不能。我们是一个封闭的、限制用户数的社区。只有注册用户才能够使用我们的 Tracker。将我们的种子文件发布到其他 Tracker 服务器是徒劳的，因为绝大多数试图下载这些文件的人将无法连接到我们的服务器。将我们的种子发布到其他 Tracker 只让那里的用户恼怒（因为无法下载）并且对我们产生敌对情绪，所以这种行为是我们是不能容忍的。 如果其他网站的管理员向我们举报我们的种子被发布在他们的站点上，对此负责的用户将因此被移出我们的社区。 如果从这里找不到我的问题的解答我该怎么办 不妨试试这个 你可以在群聊大厅或者到Telegram群组进行询问。通常情况下你能得到友善而有用的帮助。这里给你一些基本的指导： 确保你的问题的确不在这篇 FAQ 中。这样的发帖导致的结果就是返回这篇 FAQ。 在询问之前，看看置顶。很多时候，还没有被我们的 FAQ 所收录的最新的信息都可以在那里被找到。 帮助我们也就是帮助你自己。不要仅仅说“嘿我这里出问题了！！” 提供一些详情，这样我们就不用猜测或者浪费时间来询问了。你使用的是什么客户端？什么操作系统？怎样的网络设置？如果发生了错误，是什么样的具体错误信息？有问题的种子文件是哪个？你所提供的信息越多，对你的帮助也就越容易，你的帖子也就更加容易得到回复。 不需要说的是：保持礼貌。趾高气扬得命令别人帮助你很少会有用。 目录 欢迎来到 Sunny 用户信息 我可以给我的账号改个名字么 你可以删除一个已确认的账号么 违规将会失去下载权限 过低的分享率会导致严重的后果，包括禁止帐号。详见常见问题。 种子促销规则：发布员新发布的种子会free7天。 我们也将不定期开启全站免费，届时尽情狂欢吧~ 你只能使用允许的BT客户端下载本站资源。详见常见问题。 上传规则 - 谨记: 违规的种子将不经提醒而直接删除 请遵守规则。如果你对规则有任何不清楚或不理解的地方，请联系管理。管理组保留裁决的权力。 上传者资格 只有发布员能发布资源。 种子信息 所有种子都应该有描述性的标题，必要的介绍以及其他信息。以下是一份简明的规范，完整的、详尽的规范请参阅“种子信息填写规范与指导”。 标题 电影主标题：英文名 年份 分辨率 来源 动态范围(SDR可留空) 视频编码 音频编码-发布组名称 例：Avatar: Fire and Ash 2025 2160p UHD BluRay REMUX DV HDR HEVC TrueHD.7.1 Atmos-Breeze@Sunny 副标题：阿凡达：火与烬 / 阿凡达3 / 阿凡达3：火与烬 / 阿凡达3：火与灰 / 阿凡达3：带种者 / Avatar: The Seed Bearer / Avatar 3 / 2160p DV HDR /【简繁双语特效字幕】 电视剧主标题：英文名 年份 季/分集(全集可留空) 分辨率 来源 动态范围(SDR可留空) 视频编码 音频编码-发布组名称 例：Perfect Crown 2026 S01E01-E04 1080p DSNP WEB-DL AAC2.0 H264-Yobee@Sunny 副标题 21世纪大君夫人 / Perfect Crown / The 21st Century Grand Prince's Wife /【简繁双语特效字幕】 外部信息 电影和电视剧必须包含外部信息链接（TMDB/豆瓣）地址。 注意事项 管理员会根据规范对种子信息进行编辑。 请勿改变或去除管理员对种子信息作出的修改（但上传者可以修正一些错误）。 种子信息不符合规范的种子可能会被删除，视种子信息的规范程度而定。 如果资源的原始发布信息基本符合规范，请尽量使用原始发布信息。 论坛总则 - 请遵循以下的守则，违规会受到警告 禁止攻击、挑动他人的言辞。 禁止恶意灌水或发布垃圾信息。 不要为了获取魔力值而大肆灌水。 不要讨论禁忌、政治敏感或当地法律禁止的话题。 禁止任何基于种族、国家、民族、肤色、宗教、性别、年龄、性取向、身体或精神障碍的歧视性言辞。违规将导致账号永久性禁用。 评论总则 - 永远尊重上传者 无论如何，请尊重上传者！ 如果你没有下载的意向，请不要随便发表否定性的评论。 头像使用规定 - 请尽量遵守以下规则 允许的格式为.gif， .jpg， 和.png。 图片大小不能超过150KB，为了统一，系统会调整头像宽度到150像素大小（浏览器会把图片调整成合适的大小，小图片将被拉伸，而过大的图片只会浪费带宽和CPU) 。 管理守则 - 请慎用你的权限 最重要的一条：慎用你手中的权限！ 对于违规行为不要怕说“不”！ 不要公开和其他管理员冲突，一切通过私下沟通解决。 不要太绝情，给违规者一个改过的机会。 不要试图“打预防针”，等到人们犯错了再去纠正。 尝试去改正一个不适当的帖而不是简单的关闭它。 多尝试移动帖子到适合的版面而不是简单地锁帖。 当处理版聊帖的时候要宽容适度。 锁帖的时候请给予简单的操作理由。 在屏蔽某个用户前请先站短通知他/她, 如果有所积极回应可以考虑再给2周观察期。 不要禁用一个注册尚未满4周的帐户。 永远记得以理服人。 目录 总则 -
